Standalone NAV rose to Rs489/share from Rs454 a year earlier, while the market-value NAV range moved to Rs514-562 from Rs488-530. 500650|2026-09.headline: Excel Industries Q2 FY27 standalone revenue rose 1.6% to INR274.6 crore while EBITDA grew 21.5% to INR36.6 crore on a 13.3% margin.

Standalone PAT rose to INR26.7 crore from INR18.7 crore. Management flagged that agro demand will stay subdued in Q3 and that raw material volatility could pressure H2. The 5-year contract manufacturing dedicated capacity was commissioned on 23 July 2026 and is at full stream.

500655|2026-06.headline: Garware Hi-Tech Q1 FY27 revenue rose 28% YoY to INR633 crore and EBITDA margin hit a record 30.30%, with FY27 guidance reaffirmed.
500655|2026-06.overview: Management reported record quarterly revenue of INR633 crore (+28% YoY), EBITDA of INR192 crore (+56% YoY) at a 30.30% margin, and PAT of INR133 crore (+60% YoY). Management attributed the margin to product mix (Sun Control and high-IR products, architectural share) rather than one-offs, and said Q3 will be seasonally lower. Tariff refunds were excluded from Q1 and about 30-40% had been received by the call date, with the balance expected in Q2. FY27 guidance of over INR2,500 crore revenue and 25% plus/minus 2% EBITDA margin was reaffirmed; management also flagged Middle East shipping disruption that delayed some Q1 volume into Q2.

segments.name: Sun Control Films (SCF)
segments.commentary: About 55% of Q1 FY27 revenue versus 48-50% in FY26; management calls it the largest product. A new robotic SCF line (INR192 crore, about 1,200 lakh sq ft annual capacity) is due for commercial production in H1 FY28.

segments.name: Paint Protection Film (PPF)
segments.commentary: About 20% of Q1 revenue versus about 25% last year. Old PPF line runs near 100%; new line at about 60%. Some volume slipped to Q2 due to a ship stuck at Jebel Ali. Five OEM relationships including M&M.

segments.name: Architectural films
segments.commentary: Management says architectural now exceeds 25% of revenue (vs about 5% earlier, as stated) and is the highest-margin product set on like-for-like basis, per management.

segments.name: Garware Home Solutions (D2C)
segments.commentary: 9 studios operational, target 50 by end FY27. 100% direct-to-consumer; Q1 sales described as very small with no figure given. Management said D2C could exceed INR100 crore.

segments.name: Garware Application Studios
segments.commentary: Network over 250 locations in India; 14 international studios across Middle East and US.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue guidance reaffirmed at over INR2,500 crore; EBITDA margin guided at 25% plus/minus 2%. Management said 27-28% looked logical but kept the guidance.
Medium-term revenue CAGR of 15-20%; management indicated about INR3,000 crore by roughly two years out and INR3,500 crore in three to four years.
TPU line (PPF backward integration, about 75% for PPF, 25% for new products) to commission in Q3 FY27; company guides an additional 1.5-2% EBITDA margin after stabilisation in FY28.

capex_capacity: TPU line commissioning in Q3 FY27; management said it could support about INR500 crore revenue potential over three years with possible further capex.

Over INR700 crore invested in strategic expansions over recent years.
demand_pricing: US e-commerce PPF sales rising; dealer and distributor order flow described as strong in Q1.

TPU addressable market in India described by management as easily above INR1,000 crore, but it requires market creation.
Antidumping duty recommended by DGTR on TPU-based PPF imports from China.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said there were no one-offs, including tariff refunds. Margin depends on product mix (high-IR Sun Control and architectural). Q1 and Q2 are seasonally strong, Q3 lower, Q4 recovers.

qa_highlights.question: Tariff refund status and balance?
qa_highlights.answer: No refund in Q1. About 30-40% received in July-August, with full refund expected in Q2. Net benefit estimated at INR50 crore-plus after customer sharing.

qa_highlights.question: TPU line margin uplift and FY28 expansion?
qa_highlights.answer: Guidance of 1.5-2% margin uplift after the TPU line stabilises. Three TPU products are in the target list; the line is expected to add no material volume in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Current utilisation of PPF capacity?
qa_highlights.answer: Old PPF line near 100%; new line about 60%, with volume lost to Jebel Ali shipping delay expected to be recovered next quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Why not grow faster than 15-20%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the constraint is consumer and authority education and niche product positioning, not top-line demand or capacity; it does not want to commoditise Sun Control.

qa_highlights.question: Where is cash being deployed given INR850 crore balance?
qa_highlights.answer: Priorities in order: evaluate inorganic growth, more capex for integration and reliability, then growth capex. No dividend or buyback was announced; details promised in coming months.

Garware Home Solutions execution: 9 studios to 50 by FY27 end, channel partner friction, and the unquantified revenue contribution.
TPU and SCF commissioning timelines (Q3 FY27 and H1 FY28) and ramp-up.

500655|2026-06.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on results and long-term growth, but guarded on forward margins, which management repeatedly described as conservative. Evasive on specifics (GHS revenue, geography mix, R&D spend beyond a 3-5% range, capital return), often deferring to IR.

500655|2026-09.headline: Q2 FY27 revenue hit a record INR696 crore (+22% YoY) with EBITDA margin of 27.2%, and FY27 margin guidance raised 200 bps to 27% ±2%.
500655|2026-09.overview: Garware Hi-Tech Films reported its highest-ever quarterly revenue of INR696 crore, up 22% YoY and 10% QoQ, with EBITDA up 42% YoY to INR189 crore at a 27.2% margin (+377 bps YoY). PAT rose 42% to INR129 crore. H1 FY27 revenue was INR1,329 crore (+25%), EBITDA INR381 crore (+49%) and PAT INR262 crore (+50%). Management raised FY27 EBITDA margin guidance to 27% ±2% and reaffirmed revenue above INR2,500 crore, while flagging a ~INR37 crore headwind from raw material and logistics costs in the quarter.

financial_highlights.value: CPD 73%, IPD 27%; value-added products 86% of revenue

segments.name: Sun Control Film (SCF)
segments.commentary: 51% of Q2 revenue. Utilisation 75% in Q2; management expects full utilisation by Q2 FY28. Market leader with 60-65% share in India.

segments.commentary: 24% of Q2 revenue. Utilisation 73% in Q2, expected near 90-100% within about 6-12 months. Claims 60% share of Indian market; India PPF penetration ~3% of new cars.

segments.commentary: About 25% of Q2 revenue, but only 10-12% margin per management; treated as a support business for CPD films.

Tariff reversal: INR31 crore received to date (INR20 crore refunded to customers, INR11 crore booked); a further ~INR30 crore expected in Q3 (INR16 crore to books, INR14 crore to customers). Reported by reducing COGS and sales.
Inventory raised intentionally: raw materials to protect against supply disruption; export inventory days up 15-25 at customers; total 58-60 days.

qa_highlights.question: Peak revenue potential from existing capacity, and the product mix behind it?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said full utilisation of the TPU and SCF capacities could reach about INR3,500 crore; the new SCF line contributes INR450-500 crore and PPF can add about INR250 crore from current levels.

qa_highlights.question: Customer concentration (reported as 30%)?
qa_highlights.answer: Concentration exists, with one large EV customer in the US under long-term agreement; management says growth is spread across teams and that this customer does not buy architectural films.

qa_highlights.question: Crude sensitivity and the revenue impact at USD60 crude?
qa_highlights.answer: At USD100-110 crude, management said it passes through costs with a lag. Revenue would have been about INR650-660 crore instead of INR700 crore at USD60, with the lower-crude benefit mainly on the 25% crude-linked IPD business.

qa_highlights.question: Lubrizol tie-up structure and incremental top line?
qa_highlights.answer: Lubrizol supplies TPU resins and development support; 75% of TPU output goes captive into PPF (1.5-2% margin gain), and 25% goes to the market for INR75-100 crore in FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Home-solutions studio target and margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Targets of INR50 crore, INR100 crore and INR200 crore are multi-year, not one-year; D2C adds about 10-15% to margins over the roughly 40% top architectural products.

qa_highlights.question: Dividend policy?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it would convey the shareholder request to the board, citing large upcoming capex.

risks_watch: Customer concentration: one large customer, with other customers 'half that size' or one-third; management says agreements are in place.
Crude and raw material cost volatility; Q2 headwind about INR37 crore; pass-through is partial and slow for CPD.
Geopolitical disruption and the Middle East slowdown; inventory build (58-60 days) ties up working capital.

Execution risk on TPU commissioning (Q3 FY27), the SCF line (H1 FY28), and the 50-studio D2C rollout by December 2027.
A regulatory penalty of INR25 lakh from MPCB for consent validation, linked to an old boiler run during trials.

500660|2026-06.headline: GSK Pharma Q1 FY27 standalone sales rose 15% to INR924 crore and PAT 24% to INR253 crore, with growth led by innovation at 7% of sales.
500660|2026-06.overview: Standalone sales grew 15% YoY to INR924 crore, with EBITDA up 17% and EBITDA margin up 50 bps, and PAT up 24% to INR253 crore (27.6% margin). Management said about 4-5 percentage points of headline growth came from a soft base after last year's CMO supply disruption, so underlying growth was about 9-10%. Innovation products (IP-protected) reached 7% of sales versus about 4% a year ago, contributing about 4 points of growth. PAT growth included a one-off dividend from subsidiary Biddle Sawyer; excluding it, PAT growth was about 17%. Spend-to-sales rose about 1 percentage point on front-loaded promotional investment ahead of the September quarter.

financial_highlights.value: improved ~50 bps YoY (management expects ~34% range for year)

financial_highlights.change: driven by pricing and product mix
vs ~4% last year; ~4 pts of headline growth
opex up ~36% YoY per analyst question; management confirmed deliberate front-loading

segments.name: General medicines (Gen Med)
segments.commentary: Grew in double digits and most brands outgrew the market per IQVIA, with EIs of 105-106. About 44-45% of the Gen Med portfolio is under price control. Gen Med is about 2,000 field staff.

segments.name: Vaccines
segments.commentary: Held private-segment leadership in pediatric vaccines. Shingrix grew about 65% in Q1, sells about 45,000-50,000 doses per quarter, and crossed INR100 crore on a MAT basis. A phasing issue in availability for a couple of vaccines is to be corrected in Q2.

segments.name: Specialty (respiratory, oncology)
segments.commentary: Nucala has about 600 active patients, with new patient starts roughly doubling YoY to about 100-120 a month. Trelegy Ellipta holds about 10,000-12,000 units a month despite about 10-12 generic launches of umeclidinium. Zejula and Jemperli together treat about 250-300 patients a quarter.

guidance_outlook: Management does not give formal guidance; the stated objective is sustaining double-digit growth.
Opex/investment ratios expected to moderate in following quarters; S&A ratio to normalise toward historical levels through the year.
EBITDA margin expected to be roughly in the 34% range, similar to last year.
Q2 seasonal acute trends were said to be tracking in line with expectations, with June and July data supportive.
Blenrep (belantamab mafodotin, second-line RRMM) launch expected in Q2 or Q3 FY27 after DCGI approval.
Bepirovirsen (Hibsago) launch in India expected within three to four quarters.
Arexvy launch and upcoming Ojjaara expected within roughly 18-24 months.
Long-term ambition of INR8,000 crore top line in four to five years; established portfolio to grow 8-10%, with new launches providing the rest of the ~13% CAGR.
capex_capacity: Manufacturing is local-for-local: own plant at Nashik (MIDC) plus about 20 contract manufacturers; all Gen Med products are made locally. Management sees no need for further local manufacturing beyond the current portfolio.

Field force of about 2,000 in Gen Med and 200 in established vaccines; about 40-45 people in oncology (medical oncology and hematology), with new hiring focused on areas of little or no presence such as liver disease.
Blended productivity about INR15-16 lakh per rep, up 5-6% this quarter.
demand_pricing: Industry Q1 growth was about 13.5%, with volume growth around 2%; oncology was the fastest-growing Indian pharma segment at about 27%.
GSK Q1 blended volume growth was about 3-3.5%, price about 6%, and the balance from new introductions.
Acute therapies are about 60% of the Indian pharma market; Q2 (July-September) is the seasonal peak.
Supply chain: management said the worst is behind, after the CMO disruption, and that cost hardening on imported inputs from rupee depreciation has not yet hit margins.
Zejula is among the top five PARP inhibitors; Jemperli is the only approved immunotherapy in first-line endometrial cancer, which has about 17,000-19,000 new diagnoses a year.

qa_highlights.question: Does the parent's restructuring focused on specialty hurt growth and India investment, given the Gen Med-heavy portfolio?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Gen Med still grows in double digits and the parent's cost programme is a simplification effort; India was already restructured, and global trials are being brought to India to shorten launch lags.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the CMO-related lost Calpol sales have been recouped?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the worst is behind, the supply chain has been stress-tested, and business continuity plans are being strengthened. It did not quantify recovery.

qa_highlights.question: How is reach into Tier 3/4 and rural areas ensured, given peers' distributor models?
qa_highlights.answer: A super-distributor manages some tail-end brands to reach mofussil interiors; no new operating model details were given beyond this.

qa_highlights.question: What are trends for the seasonal acute Q2?
qa_highlights.answer: Trends since June are tracking in line with expectations; management expects Q2 broadly in line with its plan.

qa_highlights.question: Is the opex spike a one-off, and how should EBITDA margins be viewed?
qa_highlights.answer: Spend was deliberately front-loaded ahead of the September quarter (about 3,800 HCP events); ratios should moderate, and EBITDA margins are expected around 34%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook on Blenrep and Bepirovirsen commercialisation?

segments.commentary: Delivered highest annual profit of INR200 crore in four years and highest Q4 EBIT in ten quarters. Growth came from HX Crystal, traded ammonia and melamine exports, while caprolactam and nylon realisations were under pressure from lower global spreads.

guidance_outlook: Q1 FY27 fertilizer: raw material markets unsettled; government NBS rate revision for H1 FY27 gives a 10% uplift across nitrogen, phosphorus and sulphur nutrients to support kharif supply.
Management said there will be no production shortfall in Q1 FY27 for fertilizers, with ammonium sulphate imports arriving in the current month.

Industrial products: caprolactam-benzene spreads expected to recover, but elevated caprolactam and nylon 6 prices of Q4 unlikely to hold; melamine and technical grade urea face softer demand; export volumes expected to hold.

Fertilizer margin: DAP and urea margins expected unchanged as they are protected by government; government special package for extra DAP costs expected via circular soon; NPK grades could move plus or minus 5-10%.
IP segment expected to offset any fertilizer margin loss; caprolactam-benzene spread was above $800/MT currently versus about $670/MT in Q4.
capex_capacity: Capitalised major growth projects worth over INR670 crore in FY26, per management.
Sikka DAP train (1,300-1,400 MT/day) being converted to produce APS or DAP; completion expected in July or August 2026.
Ammonia plants 3 and 4 running at 100%; ammonia stock around 16,000 MT at Baroda complex.
Sulphuric acid tanks at full inventory level, but sulphur supply under long-term contracts (Reliance, Nayara, BPCL, IOCL) is not 100%, so imports are being sought.
demand_pricing: Fertilizer demand described as robust, supported by higher subsidy support; company running at optimum fertilizer utilisation with ammonium sulphate output at maximum possible given sulphur constraints.
Sulphur international price cited at about $850/MT; natural gas prices controlled by government, with increases absorbed through subsidy.
Melamine and technical grade urea demand soft; HX Crystal domestic demand constant; agrochemical sector absorbing geopolitical knock-on effects.
Government subsidy dues received for urea up to fourth week of April 2026 and P&K up to third week of April 2026.

qa_highlights.question: How is the organisation positioned for FY27 given geopolitical disruption and import dependence, and what consistent numbers should investors expect?
qa_highlights.answer: Management called the situation abnormal with raw material prices up manifold. Ammonia is made from domestically supplied gas at Fertilizer Nagar, where gas prices are government-controlled and absorbed via subsidy; sulphuric acid stock is sufficient for Q1.

qa_highlights.question: What is the inventory position and replenishment pipeline for raw materials?
qa_highlights.answer: Ammonia stock about 16,000 MT at Baroda with 100% plant run rates; sulphuric acid tanks full. Sulphur supply under long-term contracts is partial and expensive, so spot imports are being arranged.

qa_highlights.question: Is the company continuing ammonia trading?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes. Ammonia is imported through the company's own Sikka jetty and storage, with volumes for industry sold and ammonia traded from Jamnagar.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of the fertilizer plant changeover to produce alternative grades, and what is the outlook for each segment?
qa_highlights.answer: One DAP train at Sikka (1,300-1,400 MT/day) is being converted to produce APS or DAP; completion expected July or August 2026. Fertilizer running at optimum levels; IP spreads improved to over $800/MT from about $670/MT.

qa_highlights.question: What fertilizer per-ton margin and blended volume should be modelled?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give a precise margin given volatility. DAP and urea margins are unchanged due to government protection; NPK grades may vary by plus or minus 5-10%, offset by IP segment performance.

Government special package for DAP cost reimbursement not yet issued; margin protection depends on the circular.

Monsoon progress and possible El Nino affecting kharif demand.

500690|2026-09.headline: GSFC Q2 FY27 consolidated sales rose 49% YoY, but PBT fell 42% and PAT fell 38% as fertilizer EBIT collapsed to INR17 crores on raw material costs.
500690|2026-09.overview: Revenue hit a record Q2 on DAP realisation support, but sulfur (up 327%) and natural gas (up 62%) costs crushed fertilizer margins. Fertilizer EBIT fell to INR17 crores from INR224 crores a year earlier, while Industrial Products EBIT rose to INR66 crores from INR54 crores on better caprolactam, nylon and Anone realisations. Management said the company has no long-term debt, and it has approved a roughly INR3,000 crore phosphoric and sulfuric acid project at Sikka. H2 outlook hinges on the NBS subsidy rates for October to March, which have not yet been notified.

segments.name: Fertilizer
segments.commentary: Sales up 55% YoY (+INR1,387 crores) despite volume down 6% to 5.69 lakh MT from 6.08 lakh MT. DAP revenue rose INR1,659 crores on the government DAP special package, but EBIT fell to INR17 crores from INR224 crores.

segments.name: Industrial Products
segments.commentary: Sales up INR185 crores (30% YoY). Caprolactam sales up INR58 crores and nylon up INR60 crores on higher realisations; Anone up INR36 crores on volume; TGU up INR26 crores; melamine down INR5 crores. Caprolactam-benzene spread rose to USD 849/MT from USD 512/MT.

guidance_outlook: Management was optimistic on H2 FY27, conditional on the NBS subsidy rates for 1 October 2026 to 31 March 2027, which had not been notified at the time of the call.
Management said the Q2 profit deficit would be compensated in the next quarter if the subsidy rates are raised and approved.
Caprolactam-benzene spread is expected to moderate in Q3 FY27 as regional supply normalises.
Melamine and technical-grade urea demand expected steady; HX crystal exports may improve given subdued domestic demand.
Solar power arrangement at Sikka expected to save INR20-25 crores per quarter.
Management said no buyback or other value-creation measures have been discussed by the Board yet.
capex_capacity: Phosphoric acid and sulfuric acid (PA-SA) project at Sikka: about INR3,000 crores, EPC contract recently awarded, 30-33 months to completion. It is expected to meet 50% of DAP and NPK raw material needs captively.
C-Train modification for 1,200 MT per day APS production in place of DAP at Sikka commissioned on 23 October 2026, per market requirement.
Management estimated about 20% margin from producing phosphoric acid in-house versus purchasing it.
Rock procurement will be under a long-term contract, but contractors will not fix prices, so the price will be set at the purchase date.
demand_pricing: Rabi season opens with fertilizer inventory at the highest level in 3 years, especially urea and NPK, which intensifies competition.
Subdued southwest monsoon and low reservoir levels in southern India likely to constrain fertilizer demand.
DAP-NPK price distortion is steering farmers toward DAP, hurting NPK offtake. NBS rates are seen as key to resolving this.
Management said DAP margin is about 4% (fully compensated under the advantage/disadvantage regime) and urea margin about 3-4%. NPK margins depend on the subsidy rates still to come.

Urea subsidy receipts were received up to the third week of October. Management said urea's share of the INR3,400 crore subsidy receivable is only about INR100-300 crores, which the company expects to recover.

qa_highlights.question: What is the timeline and economics of the Sikka capex for phosphoric and sulfuric acid?
qa_highlights.answer: Project financed at about INR3,000 crores, EPC awarded, 30-33 months to complete. About 50% of DAP and NPK requirement to be captively sourced, with about 20% margin from in-house PA production.

qa_highlights.question: What is the H2 outlook given volatility?
qa_highlights.answer: Management was optimistic, citing the pending NBS subsidy rates from 1 October 2026 to 31 March 2027. It said the Q2 deficit would be made up in Q3 if rates rise, and that cost cuts under a BCG-suggested plan are being applied at Sikka.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the INR3,400 crore subsidy receivable relates to urea?
qa_highlights.answer: Urea subsidy was received up to the third week of October. Urea accounts for only about INR100-200 crores (up to INR300 crores), with the bulk tied to DAP and NPK.

qa_highlights.question: Is there any value-creation plan such as a buyback?
qa_highlights.answer: No buyback or other measures have been discussed at the Board yet; management will revert at an appropriate time.

qa_highlights.question: What is the operational efficiency gain beyond subsidy?
qa_highlights.answer: Solar power at Sikka replacing costly grid power is expected to add about INR20-25 crores per quarter.

qa_highlights.question: How is distribution and Industrial Products growth sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Fertilizer distribution is set by the government. Industrial products are sold on market demand pan-India, and management sees better IP prospects from captive raw materials and product mix, since chemical prices are not under MRP control.

Sikka PA-SA project runs 30-33 months, and its ultimate margin depends on PA and sulfur prices at commissioning.

500696|2026-03.headline: HUL Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue grew 8% with 7% USG led by volumes; EBITDA margin 23.7% at top of guidance; FY27 guided better than FY26.
500696|2026-03.overview: March quarter 2026 consolidated revenue rose 8% with 7% underlying sales growth (USG), the company's highest quarterly growth in 12 quarters, driven mainly by volume (UVG 6%). EBITDA grew 6% with margin at 23.7%, the higher end of guidance, while PAT before exceptionals was Rs 2,711 crore (+4%); reported PAT rose 20% helped by the Nutritionalab divestment versus an OZiva fair-value base effect. For FY26, turnover was Rs 63,763 crore with 5% USG and 4% UVG, and the second half outpaced the first; EBITDA grew 2% at a 23.6% margin. Management flagged a sharp March-onward rise in crude-linked input costs (8-10% material cost inflation) from the Middle East crisis and has taken 2-5% price increases, with more pricing possible.

financial_highlights.change: YoY; includes Nutritionalab divestment gain, offset by OZiva fair-value base effect

segments.name: Home Care
segments.commentary: Q4 USG 9% on high-single-digit UVG, strongest in 11 quarters; liquids grew double digit and crossed Rs 4,000 crore turnover. FY26 USG 4%.

segments.name: Beauty & Wellbeing
segments.commentary: Q4 USG 8% on mid-single-digit UVG; hair care grew strong double digit; premium skin care grew double digit while mass skin (Glow & Lovely, talc) was subdued. FY26 USG 6%. Minimalist ARR about Rs 850 crore; Simple ARR above Rs 160 crore.

segments.name: Personal Care
segments.commentary: Q4 USG 5%, pricing-led; skin cleansing grew high single digit (highest in 12 quarters) and premium cleansing bars grew double-digit volume. Oral care grew low single digit. FY26 USG 4%.

segments.name: Foods
segments.commentary: Q4 USG 5% on high-single-digit UVG; coffee grew double digit, tea grew low-single-digit volume, lifestyle nutrition grew double digit. FY26 USG 5% on mid-single-digit UVG.

Mid-term EBITDA margin guidance kept at 22.5% to 23.5%; management expects Q1 FY27 to be at the lower end given cost pressure.

Material cost inflation of 8-10% seen for the June quarter; 2-5% price increases taken so far, with further calibrated price increases in Fabric Wash and Household Care in June quarter and beyond if costs persist.
Full-year FY27 pricing not guided; management said it is too difficult to give a number.
A&P spend stepped up by Rs 270 crore in absolute terms in FY26; non-working media being optimised while core brands stay fully funded.
capex_capacity: Rs 2,000 crore capex signed off for premium formats (liquids in Home Care, Personal Care and Beauty); timeline not specified.
Rs 3,500 crore deployed in FY26 on bolt-on acquisitions including Minimalist and OZiva.

Quick Commerce customer availability up about 1,400 basis points (as shared last quarter); a dedicated Quick Commerce organisation created.
Management said it remains open to bolt-on acquisitions.
demand_pricing: Demand described as stable; rural and urban demand growing at roughly equal rates in FY26.
No pre-buying by trade ahead of March/April price increases; no restocking effect in Q4 per management.
Home Care negative UPG is anniversarising; tea volumes low-single-digit with deflation in pricing cited as the cause.
Bodywash share up about 400 bps (Nielsen-based); body wash and premium skin cleansing growing double digit.

Monsoon forecast at 92% of normal; management cited higher reservoir levels, MSP increases of 5-6%, and record government grain stocks as offsets, and expects no rural demand impact unless rainfall falls below 85%.
E-commerce grew over 25% in FY26.

qa_highlights.question: Is growth driven by volume gains after GST cuts, and what are the drivers of UVG?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited three volume buckets: market development (liquids Rs 4,000 crore, mostly volumetric), share gains on core brands, and channel capability build-out; it said elasticity gains are being reinvested.

qa_highlights.question: How confident is management on margins amid input cost volatility, and would volume priority mean margin risk?
qa_highlights.answer: Cost inflation of 8-10% on material basket versus 2-5% pricing taken so far; savings funnel accelerated; margin band of 22.5-23.5% retained, with lower end likely in the current quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Why are Home Care price hikes more modest than in the FY23 cycle?
qa_highlights.answer: Current crude-driven inflation is seen as volatile and geopolitical rather than structural, so price increases are being taken in steps; further hikes will follow if costs persist.

qa_highlights.question: Why is mass skin care dragging Beauty & Wellbeing and what is being done?
qa_highlights.answer: Glow & Lovely and talc were subdued (talc hit by seasonal weakness in March); premium skin care is growing double digit with a premium skin portfolio ARR near Rs 1,400 crore; focus on democratising new formats like sunscreen and light moisturisers.

qa_highlights.question: What is FY27 pricing outlook and Minimalist size?
qa_highlights.answer: No full-year pricing number given; Minimalist ARR is about Rs 850 crore; cosmetics sub-category growth not disclosed.

qa_highlights.question: Is there Lifestyle Nutrition sustainability given milk inflation risk?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Horlicks is consumed in water as well as milk, is focusing on nutrition benefits, and new segments (RTD, protein, Horlicks Superfoods relaunch) are still small with headroom.

Monsoon and El Nino risk to H2 rural demand; management's threshold is rainfall below 85%.
Mass skin care and Personal Care volume weakness; Personal Care grew only 5% and is pricing-led.
Price elasticity and possible down-trading if further price increases are taken; Home Care rebalancing of price and volume expected in the short term.
Horlicks/Boost recovery still early; Horlicks Superfoods national rollout and protein launch pending.
Foods remains outside the Unilever transaction perimeter; questions on the strategy alignment were addressed.

500696|2026-06.headline: HUL Q1 FY27 underlying sales growth accelerated to 10% (5% volume, 5% price), with EBITDA margin at 23% within guided range.
500696|2026-06.overview: HUL reported Q1 FY27 turnover of INR 17,184 crores with 10% underlying sales growth, the highest in 13 quarters, split equally between volume and price. Growth accelerated from 3% in H1 FY26. EBITDA rose 8% YoY to INR 3,947 crores at a 23% margin, within the guided range. Reported PAT of INR 2,680 crores fell 2% YoY because of a one-off tax credit of about INR 330 crores in the base quarter; adjusted for this, PAT grew 11%. Management reaffirmed that FY27 will be better than FY26 and that the EBITDA margin will stay around the guided range, while flagging monsoon, crude and geopolitical risks.

qa_highlights.question: Is the El Nino and monsoon risk material to growth?

qa_highlights.question: At what crude level can 23% margin be held without further price increases?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined a precise crude threshold, but said it can maintain margins with about half of inflation passed through and that crude of $75-100/bbl is manageable; $140-160 would be a different discussion.

qa_highlights.question: Is the quick commerce slowdown affecting HUL?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said QCom grew 40-50% and the channel remains structurally attractive, with new entrants and tailored assortments and pack architecture.

risks_watch: Commodity inflation (palm oil, crude-linked derivatives, tea) and the pace of calibrated pricing needed to hold 23% EBITDA margin.
Soaps volume decline under palm oil-led price pressure and value competition in soaps and liquids.
Monsoon progression (rainfall deficit cited at about 15%) and El Nino impact on rural demand.
OZiva growth moderation in Health & Wellbeing and the stated transition of the business.
Management's shift from prior quarter's language on navigating volatility to cautioning on monsoon and geopolitics; watch wording at the September Capital Markets Day.

500696|2026-09.headline: HUL Q2 FY27 underlying sales growth of 15% with 7% volume growth; PAT before exceptionals up 9% to Rs 2,795 crore.
500696|2026-09.overview: HUL reported Q2 FY27 turnover of Rs 18,071 crore, with 15% USG (its highest in 14 quarters) and 7% UVG, despite roughly 8% price growth. EBITDA margin was 22.6%, within the guided 22-24% range, down about 140 bps YoY and 40 bps QoQ as gross margin fell about 400 bps on input cost inflation. EBITDA rose 8% to Rs 4,089 crore and PAT before exceptionals rose 9%; reported PAT was flat because the base quarter had Rs 273 crore of one-off tax gains. Management said it passed through absolute cost increases, protected volumes, and offset gross margin pressure with A&P productivity and overhead leverage.

segments.commentary: USG 22% on double-digit UVG; Fabric Wash grew double digit across bars, powders and liquids. Management cut Home Care A&P by about Rs 250 crore in the quarter; segment absolute EBIT margin about 16% on revenue near Rs 7,000 crore.

segments.name: Beauty & Wellbeing
segments.commentary: USG 16% on double-digit UVG, with Hair Care accelerating. Health & Wellbeing was subdued; OZiva's 2-year CAGR is beyond strong double digits but growth is non-linear.

segments.name: Personal Care
segments.commentary: USG 9%. Skin Cleansing grew double digit with volume-led growth in Pears and Dove bars; Oral Care grew low single digit with premium innovations up double digit.

segments.name: Foods
segments.commentary: USG 9% on low-single-digit UVG. Coffee grew high single digit; mass tea was soft while Red Label Instant Tea scaled; Lifestyle Nutrition grew double digit.

guidance_outlook: Medium-term EBITDA margin expected within the current guided range of 22% to 24%; management said cyclical dips can take margin to the lower end.
Management expects commodity inflation to remain elevated, but does not expect inflation of the scale seen in June and September quarters to recur.

Kissan condiments relaunched with new packaging.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said costs are covered; tea pricing largely taken. It declined to give a numeric gross margin target and pointed to a 3 to 5 year structural improvement.

qa_highlights.question: Why has Home Care profit growth lagged strong volume growth?

qa_highlights.question: Why is Lifebuoy underperforming, and what is being done?

500710|2026-03.headline: JSW Dulux Q4 FY26 revenue rose 6.2% on 23% blended volume growth, with price and mix cuts holding back realisations and EBITDA margin near 14.4%.
500710|2026-03.overview: Management reported a record 23% blended volume growth across decorative and industrial paints, with revenue up 6.2%, the gap driven mainly by price and mix after premium price corrections from September-October 2025. Like-for-like EBITDA grew about 2% and PBT declined slightly, while the EBITDA margin was stated at around 14.4%. Management said raw material inflation since March 2026 has forced a price increase of about 9.7% through mid-May, with an estimated further 3-4% needed. The company also booked INR64.8 crore from the final real estate sale and proposed a final dividend of INR50 per share.

500710|2026-06.headline: JSW Dulux Q1 FY27 revenue rose 18.8% to ₹965 crore on ~25% volume growth, but EBITDA margin fell to 11.9% with PAT lifted by one-offs.
500710|2026-06.overview: Revenue grew 18.8% like-to-like to ₹965 crore, with volume up about 25% (about 18-19% after price). Gross margin was 37.4%, which management says was depressed by roughly 2 points of high-cost inventory and about 2.5 points from reclassifying promotional spends to gross revenue; underlying gross margin was put at 39.5-40%. EBITDA rose 14.7% to ₹115.1 crore but margin diluted about 50 bps to 11.9% after headcount additions (~160 people) and R&D investment. Reported PAT of ₹135.5 crore includes one-offs: ₹55.9 crore dividend from ICICI R&T and ₹108 crore income tax refund (incl. ₹21.5 crore interest) for AY 2013-14.

qa_highlights.question: How does volume-value gap reconcile with mix improvement?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited three factors: high-cost inventory, ~2.5% gross-to-net reclassification, and faster growth in lower-margin industrial and other businesses.

qa_highlights.question: Competitive intensity and discounting vs. new entrants?
qa_highlights.answer: Competition to remain intense for 1-2 years; company does not match new entrant discounts and benchmarks against the market leader.

qa_highlights.answer: Attributed to premium-led growth, distribution expansion, digital tools and recovery in smaller dealers after new-entrant pressure; no single driver cited.

qa_highlights.answer: July was weaker due to late rains, but management expects Q2 in a similar band and targets double-digit growth in volume and value.

500730|2026-03.headline: NOCIL Q4 FY26 revenue rose 5% QoQ to Rs.330 crore on 7% volume growth, but EBITDA margin fell to 6.4% amid raw material inflation.
500730|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue from operations was Rs.330 crore, up 5% QoQ from Rs.316 crore, with volumes up 7% QoQ, driven by domestic demand after GST 2.0 and steady single-digit international growth. Operating EBITDA fell to Rs.21 crore (6.4% margin) from Rs.27 crore in Q3, hit by gas-driven utility costs, shutdown maintenance and a Rs.7-8 crore inventory-related stock change debit. FY26 revenue fell to Rs.1,303 crore from Rs.1,393 crore, with full-year volumes up 3% and PAT down to Rs.56 crore from Rs.103 crore. Management raised prices on non-contractual business in March and on contractual business from Q1 FY27 in response to sharp raw material inflation linked to Middle East disruption.

segments.name: Domestic
segments.commentary: Domestic volumes grew single digits QoQ, aided by GST 2.0 demand; management estimates a 100-150 bps market share gain. Volume split FY26 is 70% domestic, 30% exports.

segments.commentary: International volumes grew steady single digits in Q4. Export value share is about 33% (67:33 domestic:export by value). US volumes, hit roughly 50% last quarter by duties, are recovering but management expects traction only in FY27.

segments.commentary: Specialty is about 15% of mix today, with management targeting about 20% after the new Rs.130 crore integrated specialty facility ramps up.

qa_highlights.question: Why did EBITDA not benefit from inflation given inventory on hand?
qa_highlights.answer: Legacy high-cost inventory from the prior year spilled into H1 FY26, and the FTA-driven removal of basic duty on one product compressed spreads. Q4 also had a Rs.7-8 crore stock change debit and March production cuts from gas costs.

qa_highlights.question: Will ADD on TDQ and Sulphenamides lift margins, and what are the timelines?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said quantum is premature to assess; the Finance Ministry decision is expected around mid-June, and historically exporters have absorbed duties, so net benefit is uncertain.

qa_highlights.answer: Management targets double-digit volume growth in coming years, with new products adding to volumes gradually through FY27 and not yet material.

qa_highlights.answer: Largely additional capacity, not debottlenecking; the Rs.250 crore Dahej capex volume is fully merchant. The Rs.130 crore project is partly captive intermediates. Capacity figures were not disclosed.

qa_highlights.question: Is the company still confident about cost reduction and conversion cost?
qa_highlights.answer: Utilities and other expenses fell by about Rs.10-11 crore; other expenses fell Rs.18-20 crore in FY26. No specific FY27 conversion-cost target was given.

500730|2026-06.headline: NOCIL Q1 FY27 revenue rose 20% YoY to Rs 403 crore and EBITDA margin hit 11.2%, but volumes fell 3% QoQ on supply constraints.
500730|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations reached Rs 403 crore, up 20% YoY and 22% QoQ, with volumes up 9% YoY but down 3% QoQ. Management attributed the sequential volume dip to utility and logistics constraints linked to the geopolitical situation, which pushed some orders into later quarters. EBITDA rose to Rs 45 crore (11.2% margin) and PAT to Rs 28 crore, though management described several conversion-cost items as one-offs. Anti-dumping duty on Sulphonamides (CBS and NS) was approved on 20 June 2026, while the Pilflex 13 duty awaits Government approval. FY27 guidance was set at revenue of Rs 1,400-1,600 crore and EBITDA around 10%.

500770|2026-03.headline: Tata Chemicals Q4 FY26 consolidated EBITDA fell to INR 274 crores from INR 327 crores, with a INR 1,837 crore goodwill impairment in US.
500770|2026-03.overview: Consolidated revenue fell 2% YoY to INR 3,438 crores in Q4 FY26, with EBITDA at INR 274 crores versus INR 327 crores a year earlier on subdued soda ash prices across geographies. An exceptional charge of INR 1,837 crores for US goodwill impairment (USD 208 million) and a INR 159 crores deferred tax write-off drove a loss after exceptional items. Standalone revenue rose 3% to INR 1,254 crores but EBITDA fell 6% to INR 216 crores on lower realisation. Management said the West Asia conflict raised input and shipping costs, which were largely passed through, and that the company exited unremunerative Southeast Asia exports.

500770|2026-06.headline: Tata Chemicals Q1 FY27: standalone EBITDA up 35% on volumes and FX-led soda ash pricing, while consolidated EBITDA fell about INR 100 crore on sharply lower realisations.
500770|2026-06.overview: Tata Chemicals reported Q1 FY27 with consolidated revenue up 14% YoY but EBITDA down about INR 100 crore despite lower realisations, mainly from soda ash pressure in the industrial segment. Standalone performed strongly: revenue up 10%, EBITDA up 35%, and PAT from continuing operations up 12%, helped by higher volumes, an INR 2,000/tonne soda ash price increase in India, and fixed-cost control. The company moved to three reporting segments (Living Essentials, Industrial Essentials, Farm Essentials) to highlight non-cyclical revenue, and net debt fell INR 5,692 crore QoQ on asset monetisation (management later cited about INR 300 crore of debt reduction versus March). Management flagged that cost pressures from the Middle East conflict (Kenya HFO, UK gas, India limestone and coal logistics) could intensify after October.

500770|2026-09.headline: Tata Chemicals Q2 FY27 consolidated EBITDA fell to INR381 crore (from INR537 crore) and the company posted a loss after tax of INR50 crore.
500770|2026-09.overview: Standalone revenue rose 8% YoY to INR1,303 crore and EBITDA rose 22% to INR292 crore, but standalone PAT fell 31% to INR122 crore. Consolidated results were hit by UK gas and energy cost spikes, lower overseas realisations (US exports to Southeast Asia), logistics costs, and the suspension of Kenya operations. Management described soda ash markets as oversupplied, with prices expected to stay range-bound. Net debt excluding leases stood at INR6,127 crore.

segments.name: Living Essentials (bicarbonate, salt, FOS)
segments.commentary: Standalone India volumes rose on salt, FOS and silica. The UK salt and bicarbonate operations drove the consolidated EBIT loss, from gas and energy costs and higher cost of feedstock soda ash for bicarbonate. Management expects these costs to normalise as energy and logistics costs moderate.

segments.name: Industrial Essentials (soda ash, silica)
segments.commentary: Global soda ash is oversupplied, with China as the key driver. Indian domestic prices softened late in the year, and US export pricing remains under pressure. DGTR has recommended two years of import quantity restrictions after imports rose 89% in FY2024.

segments.name: US (TCNA)
segments.commentary: Revenue rose on volumes from contracts acquired during the year, partly offset by lower export pricing. The company won Searles Valley Minerals Chapter 11 contracts covering half a million tonnes over two years. The US$22 million payment is being amortised as an intangible over five years.

segments.name: UK
segments.commentary: Revenue fell on lower salt realisation. Variable costs rose sharply on gas prices, and this was the main drag on consolidated EBIT.

segments.name: Kenya
segments.commentary: Operations have been suspended since a Ministry of Mining notice. Management says the operation is debt-free and was margin positive. The company is pursuing legal and administrative routes, and a court hearing is expected in November.

segments.name: Farm Essentials (Rallis)
segments.commentary: Monsoon shortfall and delayed sowing hurt agrochemical demand early in the period, but Kharif acreage recovered. Rallis delivered resilient performance, aided by crop care and soil health, while profitability was pressured by input cost inflation.

guidance_outlook: Near-term soda ash market expected to remain range-bound due to Chinese capacity additions and sustained export activity.
Pricing is expected to stay range-bound; sustained improvement depends on supply rationalisation and demand growth in applications and geographies.
Capex of around INR1,000 crore for the current year, including growth projects; next year expected to be roughly the same.
UK energy and logistics costs expected to moderate and return to normal levels.
Focus on cost competitiveness, supply chain resilience, working capital optimisation, debt reduction and disciplined capital allocation.
capex_capacity: Capex of around INR1,000 crore for FY27, including growth projects; FY28 expected at a similar level.
Kenya: the company had been in the midst of doubling capacity and adding a bicarbonate unit, plus seeking a partner for container glass. These plans are now affected by the suspension.
Searles Valley contracts add about half a million tonnes to be served over two years, benefiting from proximity to California and Mexico markets.
Inner Mongolia Berun's 5 million tonne phase one had maintenance outages in October, expected to return to full rates at month end (Chinese supply side).
demand_pricing: Global soda ash: persistent oversupply, weak Chinese real estate and construction demand, and high Chinese export volumes. Chinese producer inventory reached about 1.89 million tonnes by end-September.
India: demand growth remains healthy, supported by solar glass capacity and infrastructure. Imports rose 89% in FY2024 and remain elevated.
Southeast Asia exports are unremunerative; the company is serving only residual contracts and will focus on the Americas and positive-netback markets.
Farm Essentials: uneven rainfall and delayed sowing hit parts of the quarter. Cautious agricultural outlook with weather, crop prices and input costs as near-term risks.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of Kenya operations and the possible course of action?
qa_highlights.answer: Operations remain suspended after a Ministry of Mining notice. The company is pursuing administrative engagement and a legal route, citing the UK-Kenya BIT and a lease running to 2053. The Environment and Land Court is due to hear the matter in November. Management would not give a timeline for restart.

qa_highlights.question: What drives the UK-related EBIT loss in Living Essentials, and what is the outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is mainly UK salt and bicarbonate, due to higher gas and energy costs and higher feedstock soda ash logistics cost for bicarbonate. Q2 saw a sharp spike and these costs are expected to normalise.

qa_highlights.question: What contribution margins and accounting apply to the Searles Valley contracts?
qa_highlights.answer: The $22 million paid is recorded as an intangible and amortised over five years. Pricing is substantially above the export option, though exact figures were not disclosed.

qa_highlights.question: Will other US producers' shutdowns force the company to cut capacity?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Southeast Asia exports are unremunerative and it is serving only residual contracts. Strategy is unchanged and it will focus on the Americas and positive-netback markets.

qa_highlights.question: What is the nature of the INR796 crore proceeds from sale of non-current investments, and what is the capex plan?
qa_highlights.answer: The proceeds came from selling listed shares in group companies in July, used to repay US and UK debt. The company holds about INR8,000 crore of group company shares at market value. Capex is about INR1,000 crore this year and similar next year, including growth projects.

qa_highlights.question: Should the company monetise its Tata Sons stake to reward shareholders?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to comment on this.

risks_watch: Kenya suspension: outcome of the November court hearing, and the risk of losing the business or compensation through treaty arbitration.
Soda ash oversupply: Chinese export volumes, producer inventory of about 1.89 million tonnes, and possible further US capacity cuts.
UK gas and energy costs and Middle East freight volatility affecting consolidated margins.
Consolidated PAT before exceptional items and NCI was only INR10 crore in H1 FY27, against INR535 crore a year earlier.
Monitor whether Indian soda ash import quantity restrictions are imposed following the DGTR recommendation.
Net debt of INR6,127 crore excluding leases; progress on debt reduction through group stake sales.
500770|2026-09.management_tone: Candid and cautious. Management openly described the soda ash market as oversupplied and the operating environment as challenging, and was measured on Kenya, saying it is pursuing legal routes with no timeline. It was confident on India volumes and on the Searles contracts, and declined to comment on the Tata Sons stake question.
key_quotes: Despite a resilient operating standalone performance, our consolidated results were sharply impacted by natural gas cost increases in U.K.
Market conditions are characterized by persistent oversupply, subdued industrial demand, especially in China, and intense competition across export markets.
We remain committed to Kenya, we remain committed to the business, and we will do whatever is right the way we run our businesses in a very ethical and sustainable manner.

500780|2026-03.headline: Zuari Industries guides net debt to about INR700 crores by FY26-end, dependent on ~INR850-900 crore Dubai inflows over six months.
500780|2026-03.overview: Sugar operations delivered record crushing of 159.7 lakh quintal and 101.7% capacity utilisation in FY26, with sugar realisation up to INR4,053/quintal from INR3,894. Standalone PAT turned to INR12 crore from a loss of INR37 crore, and consolidated PAT was INR105 crore versus a loss of INR94.4 crore. Management says the St. Regis Dubai project (98% complete, BCC received 21 May 2026) is the main deleveraging lever, with external borrowings of about INR1,900 crore expected to fall to about INR700 crore by year-end. Ethanol remains under pressure from stagnant prices and roughly 100% industry overcapacity, and the Envien bioethanol JV is still stabilising with OMC tenders delayed.

segments.commentary: Ethanol production up 10.1% and sales up 0.7%, realisation INR62.6/litre (up 1.1%). Power sales 857 lakh units vs 907 lakh units, as the mill did not operate in April 2025.

segments.name: Zuari Infraworld (real estate DM)
segments.commentary: Total income up 78% YoY. India DM projects aggregate GDV about INR4,900 crore across Hyderabad, Kolkata (Panihati, Adventz Corporate Center) and Bangalore plotted development. Dubai St. Regis project 100% sold, 50% collected during construction, balance on BCC.

segments.commentary: Q4 income INR29.8 crore vs INR8.9 crore; FY26 income INR89.4 crore vs INR18.8 crore; FY26 EBITDA INR6.8 crore vs INR0.9 crore. About INR95 crore of projects under execution.

segments.commentary: Zuari Finserv FY26 income INR20.1 crore (up about 4.1%) and EBITDA INR5.6 crore (up about 60%). Zuari Insurance Brokers GWP INR99.4 crore (up about 9%), brokerage income INR10.2 crore (up about 40%).

segments.commentary: Plant commissioned 1 January 2026 and under stabilisation; OMC second and third round tenders have not yet been floated, with existing orders running to October.

Associate company inflow of about INR250-258 crore expected.
Management expects external borrowings of about INR700-800 crore (net debt about INR700 crore) at FY26 end, versus about INR1,900 crore currently.

Envien (ZEBPL) 180 KLPD grain-based distillery at Lakhimpur commissioned 1 January 2026, under stabilisation.
Focus shifting to steam, power and chemical consumption reduction; looking for a second UP sugar unit to complement Gobind Sugar Mill at Aira.
Development management strategy is asset-light; no land bank or joint development until about 2-3 years out.
demand_pricing: Ethanol prices stagnant; management expects revision, citing industry representations. OMC bids about 1,800 crore litres against 1,050 crore litres tendered; overcapacity now about 2,000 crore litres.
Government signals on E27, E30, E85 and E100 blending seen as positive for ethanol demand.
Input prices, including chemicals, rose in FY26; macro conditions affecting capex in India and the Middle East.
Real estate DM revenue is a fee on sales value, recognised as phases complete over about 5 years; EBITDA margin on this service revenue cited at 70-75%.

qa_highlights.question: How certain is the Dubai inflow this quarter, and how much deleveraging is expected this quarter or next?
qa_highlights.answer: Alok Banerjee said the BCC was received and demand letters are being raised; INR850-900 crore is expected over six months, with the balance of about INR800-850 crore in FY26-27 after retention money.

qa_highlights.question: What will net debt be after these inflows?
qa_highlights.answer: Jatin Jain said external borrowings of about INR1,900 crore less about INR1,200 crore of deleveraging (Dubai plus associate) leaves about INR700 crore at year-end.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Dubai project profit and capital invested?
qa_highlights.answer: Alok Banerjee said Zuari Infraworld's 50% JV share of estimated profit is about INR600 crore on capital invested of INR270-275 crore, giving about INR900 crore of cash back.

qa_highlights.question: What recourse exists if Dubai buyers default?
qa_highlights.answer: Alok Banerjee said RERA in Dubai allows forfeiture of 40% of the apartment value and resale; the timeline could be about a year, but management sees no buyer inquiries or concerns.

qa_highlights.question: Why has the value of strategic investments declined about 20%?
qa_highlights.answer: Athar Shahab said the holdings are performing operationally and management does not comment on share prices; Texmaco Rail is held as a strategic investment and not consolidated.

qa_highlights.question: What drove lower sugar recovery and what can be controlled?
qa_highlights.answer: Alok Saxena said early-season crushing starting in late October lowered the weighted average recovery; the company ranked fourth of about 14 nearby units and is replacing the 238 variety.

Currency: management says rupee depreciation is favourable for Dubai receivables; forward covers if needed.

500780|2026-06.headline: Zuari Q1 FY27 standalone loss widened to INR9.5 crore PAT on sugar margin squeeze; Dubai St. Regis repatriation of INR142.58 crore received so far against INR900 crore FY27 target.
500780|2026-06.overview: Standalone total income rose 26% YoY to INR283.9 crore on higher sugar volumes and realisations, but EBITDA fell to INR31.3 crore from INR36.9 crore and PAT swung to a loss of INR9.5 crore from a loss of INR3.9 crore. Management attributed margin pressure to an 8% rise in UP cane SAP (INR370 to INR400 per quintal). Consolidated PAT was a marginal INR0.05 crore, supported by associate income, mainly Zuari Agro Chemicals. Management reiterated the INR900 crore Dubai repatriation target for FY27 and said that sugar prices are at record highs, which it expects to support the next quarters.

qa_highlights.question: How much FY28 interest saving from repaying about INR1,100 crore of debt?
qa_highlights.answer: Jatin Jain cited 9.73% average cost of borrowing; the analyst's INR100-110 crore saving estimate was accepted on the call.

qa_highlights.question: Rationale and timing of buying Zuari International shares for INR150 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Transaction to be done in one or more tranches funded by an ICD approval; aim is to consolidate listed and unlisted group holdings into Zuari Industries and let the holding entities repay external debt.

qa_highlights.question: Will the Zuari Agro INR95 crore ICD get a six-month extension, and when will the INR258 crore be repaid?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not confirm any extension; said the entire INR258 crore outstanding is expected to be repaid in the current quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Will ethanol capacity expand, and are OMC tenders expected?
qa_highlights.answer: Next OMC tender expected in October 2026 and the company will participate; capex on hold due to overcapacity (1,050 crore litres tendered vs 1,800 crore litres offered), with investment only after demand clarity.

qa_highlights.question: Why did standalone EBITDA fall despite revenue growth, and why did sugar segment profit drop?
qa_highlights.answer: UP cane SAP rose 8% (INR370 to INR400 per quintal); extra one lakh quintal of sugar sales from higher quota added about INR45 crore revenue, but segment profit fell to INR8.4 crore from INR12.3 crore on cane cost.

qa_highlights.question: Sustainability of earnings of sugar, power and ethanol over next 12-18 months?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects the segments to recover in the next season, cites high sugar prices and a healthy UP cane crop, and expects a fairly decent quarters ahead.

qa_highlights.question: Concern over Texmaco share purchase at INR190 and shareholder value?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the earlier Zuari International transaction was only an enabling resolution with no actual deal; future transactions will be at market price.

qa_highlights.question: Dubai repatriation, buyer payments and segment asset timing at Zuari Infraworld?
qa_highlights.answer: Alok Banerjee said about 40-45% of customer collections remain; payment plan is 50-50 and demand notes were raised post completion certificate. Real estate segment assets of INR770 crore as on 30 June 2026, mainly INR400 crore Dubai receivables, expected to convert in one to two quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Zuari Infra DM pipeline and GDV path to INR10,000 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Order book about INR6,000 crore per Alok Banerjee; GDV of projects in hand about INR4,900 crore per Athar Shahab, roughly halfway to the INR10,000 crore aspiration; Hyderabad and Bengaluru launches next month; plotted project cycle time 15-18 months.

Management guided to 50-75 bps full-year margin expansion in FY27, double-digit top-line growth, and a stepped-up A&P ratio of 7.5-8.5%.

500820|2026-09.headline: Asian Paints Q2 FY27: decorative volume grew 6.4% and value 14.5%, while gross margin dipped to 41-43% band guidance and PBT margin fell to ~4.8% on inflation lag.

500825|2026-03.headline: Britannia Q4 FY26 revenue rose 7.1% to INR 4,686 crore, with PAT up 21.1% to INR 678 crore helped by a tax case release.

500825|2026-09.headline: Britannia Q2 FY27 revenue rose 16.6% YoY to INR 5,542 crore, with PAT at 13% of revenue and H1 revenue crossing INR 10,000 crore.
500825|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue from operations was INR 5,542 crore, up 16.6% YoY and 11.6% QoQ, with PAT up 10.2% YoY and 13% margin on revenue. H1 revenue was INR 10,506 crore (up 13.1%), the first time H1 crossed INR 10,000 crore. Volume growth was 13% on a low base of minus 3%, and General Trade (GT) accelerated, with management attributing part of this to a GST transition base effect worth 1.5-2%. Input costs (wheat flour, palm oil, sugar, milk, laminate, fuel) rose sharply YoY, and a 3.5% price increase was implemented in the quarter with more in the pipeline.

financial_highlights.value: Growth as stated 8.5% YoY; management cited operating profit margin around 17%

segments.name: General Trade (GT)
segments.commentary: GT growth in Q2 FY27 is 2.6x the full-year FY26 growth rate, per management; GT is the largest part of the business. Growth described as uniform across opportunity and mature states, with rural and semi-urban strong.

segments.name: E-commerce
segments.commentary: E-commerce is trending at close to 7% of overall sales (FY26 about 6%); management says it would be in double digits excluding INR 5 pack sales, and the company is treating it as a separate business unit.

segments.name: Other channels (modern trade, alternate, e-commerce)
segments.commentary: Growing at a rate significantly above GT, per management.

segments.name: Adjacency bakery business
segments.commentary: Grew more than 20%, led by croissant and cake; rusk growing slower. Dairy: cheese performing better (flavoured slices launched about 1.5 months earlier); Sattvam Ghee and Winkin' Cow milk drink trending well.

segments.name: International
segments.commentary: Recovered after Q1 disruption from Middle East war; Middle East Africa and rest of International both grew in good double digits, though Middle East costs remain high due to freight premiums.

segments.name: Biscuits share of portfolio
segments.commentary: Biscuits about 78-80% of total sales, with non-biscuit portfolio expected to grow faster.

guidance_outlook: Further price increases (activation/shrinkflation-led) are in the works; the 3.5% taken in the quarter covers only part of cost inflation, and management aims to close the gap with subsequent increases; implementation takes about 1.5-2 months.
Management declined to guide on future gross margin trajectory, saying inflation is expected to persist and events are hard to predict.
Grammage reduction is expected to weigh on volumes going ahead, though management remains confident in the volume growth story.

Cost optimisation programmes to continue this year to limit pass-through to consumers.

Women make up 45% of factory workforce; Britannia Nutrition Foundation reached about 5.73 lakh beneficiaries in H1.
demand_pricing: Input costs YoY: wheat flour marginally down; refined palm oil up 17%; sugar up 6%; milk up 16%; laminate up 18%; fuel up 45%. QoQ: wheat flour up 9%, palm oil up 11%, sugar up 4%, milk up 2%, laminate up 7%.
Price increase of 3.5% implemented in Q2; further increases planned. Industry migrated from INR 4.5 fractional pricing to INR 5 and INR 10 price points around May-June 2026.
Management says shelf space has been regained versus Malkist and others after odd-pricing period; NutriChoice Zero growing in strong double digits.

Competition: Malkist (cracker segment, Cheeze Dipped launched by Britannia to compete), and Reliance entering biscuits starting in Tamil Nadu; management says INR 5 and INR 10 price points are harder to disrupt than in cola.
GST-related transition in September last year contributed a base effect of at most 1.5-2% at quarter level.

qa_highlights.question: Are there further price increases beyond the 3.5% taken, and how should gross margins evolve?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 3.5% came through, more price increases are in the works, and the 3.5% covers only part of inflation; it declined to predict gross margin direction.

qa_highlights.question: Is the GT pickup a base effect or sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Partly base effect (September transition month, impact up to 1.5-2% of quarter), but management also cited resilient GT consumption in semi-urban and rural areas and better own execution; Vipin Kataria said growth is uniform and sustainable.

qa_highlights.answer: Yes; management said Britannia has regained shelf space and share, and the INR 4.5 price point has disappeared from the market.

qa_highlights.answer: E-commerce at about 7% of sales; management is treating it as a business unit with channel-specific products and sees premiumisation as the key lever; urban e-commerce already in double digits.

qa_highlights.question: How do you see wheat coverage and the next crop?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Britannia is an efficient wheat buyer, has historically beaten the market with mark-to-market gains, and is watching a challenging monsoon for the next wheat season; no specific coverage percentage given.

qa_highlights.question: Biscuit vs non-biscuit mix and medium-term growth shape?

Foreign business (about 50% of Q4 business historically) hit by West Asia war; management expects the impact to be limited in summer months, with foreign travel peaking October to March.
Management expects a big summit in Q2 and Q3 FY27 to benefit demand, following AI Summit benefit in February-March.
Capex of about Rs 600-700 Cr a year to continue for the next one to two years, rising in FY29-30 when larger hotels open.

Oberoi Grand Kolkata (about 200 keys) renovation under way with structural works; reopening targeted September 2026. Oberoi Grand Kolkata cited as timeline issue; separately, Oberoi Gandikota site delay moved from 2028 to 2030 due to site change.

Renovations: about 90 rooms at Oberoi Bangalore in 18-room blocks over summer; Trident Nariman Point 4 floors (six months); 4 floors at Oberoi Mumbai one floor at a time; F&B overhaul at Trident Bandra Kurla later in FY27.
demand_pricing: Q4 industry occupancy 67-69%, below last year on West Asia war impact; industry ARR up 6-8% and RevPAR up 5-7%. FY26 industry occupancy flat, ARR up 9-10%, RevPAR up 10-12%.

Occupancy weakened through Q4 with a sharp drop in March; ARR for EIH owned hotels rose from Rs 24,548 to Rs 28,198 in Q4. January RevPAR negative (about -6%), which management attributed to unexplained weak demand, possibly negative international press on air quality.
Delhi/NCR, Mumbai (T20 World Cup) and Bhubaneswar grew strongly; Bangalore hit by lower foreign bookings; Udaipur down on fewer weddings.
Room revenue: MICE and direct segments grew; corporate and leisure flat.
Management says India is significantly underpriced versus Europe, North America and parts of Asia at the top end; no reason to discount rates given rate premium strategy.

qa_highlights.question: What drove February ARR growth near 25% and why was January RevPAR negative?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said January was weak, with promotions having limited effect; the likely cause (unvalidated) was negative international press on North India air quality. February was strong, helped by the AI Summit, deferred winter travel and strong demand across leisure and city hotels.

qa_highlights.question: With few owned key additions in FY27-28, what drives growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Two levers: ARR (premium positioning, headroom if market stays buoyant) and cost elimination of waste rather than cuts. No specific growth guidance was given.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Q4 flight catering (OFS) revenue and was it new clients?
qa_highlights.answer: About Rs 145 Cr in Q4, mainly existing airlines expanding flights and market share, including some domestic airlines.

qa_highlights.question: Where do foreign tourist mix and Q4 FTA levels stand?
qa_highlights.answer: Q4 foreign business about 50% historically; domestic share rose substantially in March and more than offset weaker foreign demand. Exact March quarter mix to be shared offline.

qa_highlights.question: Was there a financial loss from geopolitical issues in Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: No financial impact calculated; lower foreign room nights were offset by domestic business.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other expenses rise about 20% in Q4 and will Mashobra O&M continue?
qa_highlights.answer: Higher expenses from business growth, higher airport levy on OFS, higher R&M, CSR, legal and donation costs. Mashobra case settled in June; hotel operated until October 2026.

risks_watch: Margin pressure: Q4 EBITDA only 1% growth as OFS mix rises and airport levy and wage code costs increase; watch for margin recovery in FY27.
Managed hotel project slippage (Trident Goa, Dehradun, Rishikesh and others); management says owners control timelines and delays are not significant, but 2027 pipeline looks thin.
Oberoi Grand Kolkata renovation: structural issues found, reopening target September 2026 still stated; any change would be updated to the board and investors.
Oberoi Rajgarh (Khajuraho) connectivity: only seasonal Delhi flights; no flights expected July-September unless IndiGo extends.
Geopolitical risk: West Asia war impact on foreign travel and occupancy; the company has not quantified the impact; March occupancy weakness may persist into Q1 FY27.
Supply risk in FY29-30 from new luxury keys in some micro-markets; management says the rate premium will be maintained rather than discounted.
500840|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on long-term demand and pipeline but cautious on near-term occupancy; management acknowledged a challenging year and avoided forward numbers, deferring several specifics (foreign mix, flight catering split, consolidated room revenue) to offline follow-up.

500840|2026-06.headline: EIH Q1 FY27 revenue rose 15% to Rs 698 crore and PAT to Rs 120 crore, but EBITDA grew only to Rs 207 crore as margin fell on Rajgarh ramp-up and one-offs.
500840|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue rose 15% YoY to Rs 698 crore (Rs 609 crore) and EBITDA rose to Rs 207 crore from Rs 195 crore, so margin compressed. Management attributed the gap to Oberoi Rajgarh ramp-up, about Rs 4 crore of extra marketing, IT/automation spend, power and fuel inflation from the West Asia conflict, and Rs 6-7.5 crore of renovation write-offs at Mumbai hotels. Growth was domestically led as foreign arrivals fell about 10% in Q1. Standalone numbers were stated to mirror consolidated. PAT of Rs 120 crore is not comparable with last year, which carried a Rs 110 crore Mashobra one-time impact.

500840|2026-09.headline: EIH Q2 FY27: consolidated revenue up 16%, EBITDA up 19%, PAT up 21% to ₹153 cr as RevPAR grew ~18% on ARR gains.
500840|2026-09.overview: Management described Q2 as a good quarter, with consolidated revenue up 16% YoY, EBITDA up 19% and net PAT of ₹153 cr versus ₹142 cr a year earlier. Industry occupancy rose 1-3% and ARR 8-10%, and EIH's RGI improved from 121% to 130%. Renovations at Mumbai hotels cut inventory and pulled occupancy down to 71% from 74% on total rooms, while ARR growth drove RevPAR up 18.3%. Cash reserves stayed above ₹1,100 cr, with H1 capex of roughly ₹400 cr largely offset by operating cash flow.

500850|2026-03.headline: IHCL Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue rose 14% to INR2,845 crores with EBITDA margin of 37%; FY27 guidance is double-digit (12-14%) revenue growth.
500850|2026-03.overview: IHCL reported its 16th consecutive quarter of record performance, with Q4 consolidated revenue up 14% YoY to INR2,845 crores and EBITDA up 15% to INR1,052 crores. Standalone Q4 RevPAR grew 12%, the company said, with standalone EBITDA margin up 160 bps to 49.5%. For FY26, consolidated revenue grew 16% to INR9,971 crores and consolidated PAT crossed INR2,000 crores for the first time. Management said March and early April were weak due to the West Asia conflict, with recovery from mid-April, and guided FY27 revenue growth of 12-14%, with Q1 FY27 growth expected above 12%.

500850|2026-06.headline: IHCL Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 15% to INR2,419 crores and PAT 21% to INR358 crores, with EBITDA margin at 31.1%.
500850|2026-06.overview: IHCL reported its 17th consecutive quarter of record performance, with consolidated revenue up 15% YoY to INR2,419 crores, EBITDA up 18% to INR753 crores and PAT up 21% to INR358 crores. Domestic RevPAR grew 14% and hotel segment revenue 17%, driven by leisure markets like Rajasthan and Goa while international properties, especially Dubai, lagged due to West Asia disruption. Standalone revenue grew 18% to INR1,298 crores with EBITDA up 30% to INR542 crores and margin of 41.8%. Management reiterated double-digit revenue growth for the year and said July and early Q2 trends were strong.

financial_highlights.change: c.+6 pts YoY (analyst cited 35% to 39%ish; mgmt said margin up 0.5%)

segments.name: Hotels
segments.commentary: Hotel segment revenue grew 17% and makes up about 87% of business; domestic RevPAR grew 14%, with double-digit RevPAR growth across all brands. Margin held at 32.6% despite about INR15 crores of Frankfurt ramp-up and TajSATS Noida kitchen costs.

segments.name: Growth brands (Ginger, Qmin, ama, Tree of Life)

segments.commentary: Brij's 11 operational hotels generated INR11 crores revenue, up 42% YoY. Atmantan delivered INR19 crores consolidated revenue, up 19% YoY.

qa_highlights.question: Are MICE and domestic demand shifts from international travel accelerating into H2?

qa_highlights.question: Why did standalone employee cost rise only 0.6% YoY?

qa_highlights.question: Will full-year growth reach the upper end of 12-14% guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q2 is tracking ahead, with July stronger than Q1; it hopes to beat, but gave no explicit guidance raise.

qa_highlights.question: How will Frankfurt be accounted for?
qa_highlights.answer: Full revenue is booked; the asset's impact turns positive from September, after pre-opening costs in July and August.

qa_highlights.question: What is the international strategy and capital intent?
qa_highlights.answer: Capital-light model only, with no hotel purchases; leases on institutional-style returns of 5-7% and brand-led renovations in Singapore, Switzerland and London.

500850|2026-09.headline: IHCL raised FY27 consolidated revenue growth guidance to 15%-17% after Q2 revenue rose 22% to INR2,484 crores and standalone EBITDA margin hit 38.9%.
500850|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 was strong: consolidated operating revenue grew 22% YoY to INR2,484 crores, operating EBITDA grew 24% to INR706 crores (28.4% margin, up 50 bps), and PAT rose 23% to INR349 crores. Standalone operating revenue grew 26% to INR1,336 crores and standalone EBITDA grew 40% to INR520 crores, with margin up 400 bps to 38.9%. Management raised FY27 consolidated revenue growth guidance to 15%-17% from 12%-14%, with Hotel segment growth of 17%-19%. Occupancy rose to 82% from 75%, and TajSATS remained a drag on margins.

segments.commentary: Income up 25% to INR156 crores, driven by 25% growth in managed room inventory, higher RevPAR, technical fees and new brand fees from branded residences and villas; management targets high-teens fee CAGR.

segments.name: Select service (Ginger, Qmin, Ama, Tree of Life)
segments.commentary: Ginger revenue INR193 crores (+25%) at 40% EBITDA margin; Ginger reached 100 operational hotels and targets 150 by March 31, 2027. Qmin has over 130 outlets, Ama over 400 villas and bungalows, Tree of Life over 50 resorts.

segments.name: TajSATS (air catering)
segments.commentary: EBITDA declined sequentially in Q2 due to airline schedule curtailments after West Asia fuel-price pressure; non-aviation institutional catering partly offset the decline. Management expects improvement in H2.

H1 FY27 capex is 20%-30% above the annual average of the preceding 7-8 years, per management.

Asset upgrades at Taj Palace New Delhi, President Mumbai, Taj West End Bengaluru, Taj Fort Aguada and Taj Lake Palace; Taj Palace New Delhi room revenue up 132% YoY and crossed INR100 crores monthly revenue in September.
Expected upcoming Frankfurt ramp-up after start-up challenges; London and San Francisco expected to improve in Q3.

Demand supported by MICE events (BRICS Summit, Bloomberg event, fintech event); management said Q2 ex-BRICS would still have been a comfortable double-digit RevPAR number.
Wedding nights next year are expected at about 95 versus 60-65 normally, a tailwind for social MICE.
Domestic demand is the main pillar; foreign tourist arrivals have a 3.9% 10-year CAGR, and management sees upside if this reaches 5%-6%. Room nights were flat YoY in Q2 per management.

Tier 2/3 supply: management says demand growth of 15%-20% in these markets is largely met by unorganised players, and that the 12% capacity CAGR headline should be viewed with caution given project delays.

qa_highlights.question: What drives the H2 guidance implied by the revised numbers, and is occupancy at 82% sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said growth will be mostly rate-led plus new hotels and international recovery (London, Pierre, San Francisco, Frankfurt), with occupancy gains also in the mix; H2 guidance is conservative given the 30-34 hotel openings.

qa_highlights.question: Why did TajSATS EBITDA fall sequentially?
qa_highlights.answer: Airline schedule curtailments after West Asia fuel-price pressure, mainly from June; Q2 had the full impact. Non-flight catering grew, but at lower margin. FY27 is a consolidation year.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 14% implied H2 growth conservative and what are the uplift drivers?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said H2 growth would have to be higher than the 14% arithmetic to hit guidance, given TajSATS drag, a high Q4 base and seasonally strong MICE and weddings.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 25% growth in Q2 driven by renovation base effects?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said renovations are routine for iconic assets; H1 capex is 20%-30% above normal and the growth reflects structural demand shifts, not only a low base.

qa_highlights.question: Why keep international assets, given lower margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited strategic value of the global Taj brand; international consolidated margin of about 35% is stated as industry-leading, with London profitable and Pierre EBITDA-positive but not at 20%-25% margins.

qa_highlights.question: What can standalone RevPAR be without BRICS, and how sustainable is the 400 bps margin expansion?
qa_highlights.answer: No one-offs in Q2; margin gain from operating leverage, MICE, and management fee mix (booked standalone). Management did not give specific margin guidance but expects a positive margin trend despite new payroll and regulatory costs.

500870|2026-03.headline: Castrol India Q1 FY26 revenue rose 9% to INR1,545 crore and EBITDA 7% to INR329 crore, with management flagging raw-material cost pressure from Q2.
500870|2026-03.overview: Castrol India reported Q1 FY26 revenue of INR1,545 crore (up 9%), EBITDA of INR329 crore (up 7%) and PAT of INR242 crore (up 4%), with volume growth of 7-8% YoY. Management said the Middle East conflict and weaker rupee (about 6.5-7% down YoY) began to hit costs late in the quarter, but minimal raw-material inflation reached Q1 COGS because of inventory cycles. One round of price increases was taken at end-March, and the bulk of raw-material cost increases is expected in Q2. Operating expenses rose sharply QoQ, which management attributed partly to one-time employee costs expected to fall in coming quarters.
