segments.name: Industrial
segments.commentary: Growing at double-digit for multiple consecutive quarters; weighted-average margin is lower than automotive, though some niche applications are high margin.

segments.name: Service network
segments.commentary: 800 Castrol Auto Services at end-March; 34,000 independent bike workshops and 13,000 multi-brand car workshops reached.

guidance_outlook: Structural EBITDA margin band of 21-24% retained as the target; management said Q1 is seasonally the softest quarter and Q1 margin dilution was not large.
Raw-material cost increases (crude, packaging, fuel, additives) expected to flow into COGS from Q2 FY26; one round of pricing taken end-March, with further price-plus-cost-cut actions possible.
One-time employee costs in Q1 opex are expected to decline, so future quarterly opex should be lower than Q1 levels.
Parent-level deal remains subject to global regulatory approvals; management says there is no change to Castrol India's structure, strategy or operating model.
No guidance given on data-centre cooling opportunity.
capex_capacity: No capacity, capex or utilisation figures were discussed on the call.
Base oil sourced from Indian refiners, Singapore and South Korea; imports driven by specification needs, and the company is open to other sources.
Term base-oil contracts are index-linked (Argus and ICIS); no scarcity premium reported as of call date.
MoU signed with Hindustan Petroleum Corporation to explore a re-refined base oil ecosystem in India.
Data-centre cooling (immersion and direct-to-chip) is at trial stage in India; no timeline or market size given.
demand_pricing: Hedging: 60-day policy linked to inventory cycle; about half of COGS is locally sourced (not hedged) and half imported (USD exposure hedged).
Pricing: no blanket increase; price changes set product by product to recover cost increases, with intent to hold margins.
Rural margins described as accretive, with premium bike oils (Activ) carrying high gross margins; car margins highest, then bikes, then CVs.
Competition in EV space: partnerships with Ather Energy (2W) and Tata Mobility (EV transmission fluids), with products for hybrid, E20 and gas engines already in market.
Middle East sourcing pressure: higher cost and less predictable lead times for feedstocks; no material supply disruption yet.

qa_highlights.question: Has the crude price spike in March flowed into Q1 raw-material costs, and how fast can price increases pass through?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said minimal raw-material impact hit Q1 COGS due to inventory cycles, with the main impact being FX; most cost increases are expected in Q2. One round of pricing was taken at end-March.

qa_highlights.question: Why did operating expenses rise about 23% QoQ and 10% YoY, and what is the run-rate?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said total expenses grew 9%, in line with revenue, and COGS grew slower than volume. Some one-time employee costs sit in the quarter and should fall, so future quarters should be lower than Q1.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 7-8% volume growth YoY or QoQ?
qa_highlights.answer: Management confirmed it is Q1 FY26 versus Q1 FY25, YoY.

qa_highlights.question: What EBITDA margin should be expected for the year, given the drop to about 21%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reiterated the 21-24% operating EBITDA band. Q1 is seasonally soft and not heavily diluted, but short-term volatility could come as raw-material costs rise.

qa_highlights.question: Are base-oil prices showing a premium or scarcity pricing?
qa_highlights.answer: Contracts are index-linked to Argus and ICIS, which have moved up. No separate scarcity premium is applied to term contracts.

qa_highlights.question: What is the data-centre opportunity, its timeline and its market size?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the work is beyond pilot, with trials under way in India, but gave no timeline, guidance or market size because technology choices are not yet firm.

qa_highlights.question: Which segment is pulling down overall volume growth despite double-digit growth in rural and premium urban?
qa_highlights.answer: Large commercial vehicle business, including truck engine oil, plus specialty products such as transmission fluids and greases, grew high single-digit, which pulls the blended rate to 7-8%.

risks_watch: Raw-material and feedstock cost inflation (crude, packaging, additives) and FX pressure from Q2 FY26, with only one price increase taken so far.
Margin band: whether EBITDA stays within 21-24% as the pricing and cost-cut response plays out.
Sustainability of opex: confirm that one-time employee costs decline in Q2 and beyond.
Middle East sourcing: lead-time unpredictability and possible supply gaps despite diversified sourcing.
Parent-level transaction: regulatory approvals pending; management says no operating change at Castrol India.
500870|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on Q1 execution and earnings quality, but noticeably cautious on the outlook: management repeatedly flagged near-term volatility and cost pressure from Q2. Answers on pricing quantum, the one-time cost amount and data-centre timelines were evasive or non-quantified.
key_quotes: We have delivered our 12th consecutive quarter of stable revenue and volume growth.
Given the inventory cycle, we saw minimal impact of these raw material increases into the COGS that we reported in quarter 1.
Structurally, we will recover the structural margin for the company, we will want to go back into that same range of 21%, 24%.
So, we don't see rural as a gross margin dilutor for us at all.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management expects raw-material cost increases (crude, packaging, additives, FX down about 6.5-7% YoY) to hit COGS from Q2, with only one price round taken at end-March; the 21-24% EBITDA band is held but short-term volatility is flagged, and Q1 EBITDA margin was about 21% (INR329 crore on INR1,545 crore revenue).

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Q1 FY26 volume grew 7-8% YoY with rural and premium urban growing double digit, though the CV and specialty range grew only high single digit; no volume guidance was given, so the call rests on the recent run-rate.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: No revenue or margin guidance raise was signalled; management reiterated the 21-24% band and flagged cost pressure from Q2 that is expected to weigh on margins.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Raw-material cost increases are expected to flow into COGS from Q2 with only one price round (end-March) taken so far, and pricing quantum and the one-time employee cost amount were not quantified, so the margin band could come under pressure.

rows.label: Further price-plus-cost-cut actions in response to raw-material inflation
rows.why: Management said further price-plus-cost-cut actions are possible after the one round taken end-March, with raw-material costs (crude, packaging, additives) flowing into COGS from Q2 FY26; quantum was not disclosed.

rows.label: Decline in one-time employee costs in opex
rows.why: Opex rose about 23% QoQ to about INR338 crore partly on one-time employee costs that management expects to fall in coming quarters, though the amount was not quantified.

tone.note: Management was confident on Q1 execution (revenue +9%, volume +7-8%) but cautious on Q2 raw-material cost pressure and the margin outlook; pricing quantum, the one-time cost amount and data-centre timelines were not quantified.

500870|2026-06.headline: Castrol India Q2 CY26 revenue rose 25% YoY to INR1,871 crore and EBITDA 41% YoY to INR494 crore, helped by inventory benefits and pricing.
500870|2026-06.overview: Castrol India reported strong Q2 (April–June 2026) with revenue from operations of INR1,871 crore (+25% YoY, +21% QoQ), EBITDA of INR494 crore (+41% YoY and QoQ) and PAT of INR348 crore (+43% YoY). Growth was described as broad-based across consumer, industrial and institutional businesses, with two price increases in January–June 2026 and some benefit from older, lower-cost inventory. Management said cost inflation from supply disruptions and commodity volatility began to hit late in the quarter and will be more visible in Q3. The company declared an interim dividend of INR6.25 per share.

segments.name: Consumer (B2C, retail/auto care)
segments.commentary: Broad-based volume growth driven by rural operations and urban premiumisation; POWER1 (premium motorcycle) grew ahead of rest of business. Rural business growing at double digits; rural outlets ~45,000.

segments.name: Industrial
segments.commentary: Growing at high double digits over last couple of years; about 15% of overall business per CFO. Growth from advanced solutions and expanded customer base.

segments.name: Institutional / B2B (OEMs)
segments.commentary: Works with OEMs such as Tata Motors and Maruti; growth tied to OEM volumes. No separate figures disclosed.

guidance_outlook: EBITDA margin management framework remains 21%–24%; pricing actions are set to keep margins within this band.
Commodity and feedstock inflation expected to become more visible in Q3 FY27, with some raw material increases expected to spill over into Q3.
Management says price actions taken so far are sufficient to offset raw material increases from Q2, but will take further pricing if base oil or FX move adversely.
Lubricant industry expected to grow 3%–4%; company aims to grow at about 2x market.
Capex of about INR100 crore per year, roughly half in manufacturing and half in market (dealer/workshop visibility).
Sourcing guidance of ~55% domestic / ~45% imported broadly unchanged, with quarterly tactical variation.
capex_capacity: Annual capex of about INR100 crore, split roughly equally between manufacturing (health, safety, capacity) and in-market investments.
Silvassa plant was shut for a few days in July 2026 due to heavy rain; fully back up with operating levels at Q2 peak per management.
Paharpur and Silvassa plants completed 9 years and 3 years respectively without significant recordable incident.

National footprint of ~160,000 outlets; auto care range in 40,000 outlets; 34,000 independent motorcycle workshops and 16,000 car workshops; 850 Castrol Auto Service (CAS) outlets; 950 rural service express units.
Building capabilities for specialised EV fluids and data-centre cooling fluids; data-centre business not yet material.
demand_pricing: Two price increases taken in January–June 2026 (late Q1 and Q2), in the low double-digit percentage range; pricing aimed at offsetting supply chain volatility and inflation.
Volume growth described as broad-based across consumer and industrial; company declined to disclose absolute volume (million litres) for the quarter, departing from past practice of sharing it.
Competitor reportedly took around 4 price increases between March and July 2026; management said it will not follow competitor pricing blindly and is guided by RM outlook and margin band.
Group III base oil prices elevated, impacted by Middle East crisis.
Inventory: about half of raw materials bought locally and half from international suppliers; company says it runs lean inventory and that Q2 benefited from older, cheaper inventory being consumed.
E20 fuel: most passenger car brands already compliant; impact on lubricants seen as limited to engine-level fuel-choice issues.

qa_highlights.question: Timeline for the open offer linked to the BP/Stonepeak Castrol global divestment?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the deal is progressing but is large and multi-country; open offer timing depends on deal closure, after which SEBI and shareholder notifications and prescribed timelines apply. No timeline given.

qa_highlights.question: Volume vs pricing split and Silvassa flood impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Volume growth is broad-based but no specific figures given; price increases were in low double digits. Silvassa plant was halted briefly in July for safety and is now at peak operating levels, with no impact.

qa_highlights.question: Was there an inventory gain in Q2?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said older inventory bought at softer prices was consumed in the quarter, benefiting margins; it declined to quantify and said profitability grew healthily even excluding this.

qa_highlights.question: Dividend policy?
qa_highlights.answer: No fixed payout percentage; dividend yield usually around 5% including interim and final; special dividends given occasionally. Interim window was advanced this year. Past three years' payout has been in the 80%–90% range per the questioner, which management did not confirm as policy.

qa_highlights.question: Why are price hikes not enough to offset Q3 raw material cost, given diesel prices fell after June?
qa_highlights.answer: Pricing was modelled on inventory and FX scenarios for Q2 and H2; current pricing is seen as broadly reflecting Q3 costs, but the environment is volatile and further price action is possible. Structural cost reductions are also underway.

qa_highlights.question: OCI loss of ~INR66 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: It is a fair-value revaluation of the Ki Mobility investment made about 4 years ago, using listed comparable companies, reviewed every six months; expected to move up and down with peers.

risks_watch: Commodity and base oil (Group III) cost inflation expected to hit Q3 margins more visibly; margin band 21%–24%.
Foreign exchange movements affecting input costs.
Possible volume trade-off or downtrading from the price increases, especially with competitor pricing reportedly higher.
Dependence on Silvassa plant and monsoon/weather disruptions.
Pending BP/Stonepeak divestment of Castrol global, with open offer timing uncertain.
Lack of volume disclosure reduces visibility into volume vs price split.
500870|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on the quarter's results and the broad-based growth story, but cautious on the outlook, citing inflation, volatility and monsoon conditions. Management was evasive on volume figures, inventory gain quantification, the open offer timeline and data-centre revenue.
key_quotes: And this is in context of a very volatile operating environment marked by supply disruptions and commodity cost inflation.
We, therefore, expect the impact of commodity and feedstock inflation to become more visible in the third quarter.
I think we pride ourselves on a very lean inventory profile.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: EBITDA margin was ~26% in Q2 but management holds a 21%-24% band, cost inflation from base oil and FX to be more visible in Q3, and Q2 was helped by older cheaper inventory that will not repeat.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: No new plant, line or capacity addition was announced; Silvassa was only down for a few days in July and is back at peak, and capex is held at about INR100 crore per year split evenly between manufacturing and in-market.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management targets about 2x the lubricant industry's 3%-4% growth, roughly 6%-8%, backed by two low-double-digit price rises, though absolute volume was not disclosed.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capex is held at about INR100 crore per year with no new plant or board-approved expansion, and the call gave no utilisation figure to suggest a step-up is needed.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Margin band and volume aim were both held rather than raised, and management said Q3 cost inflation will be more visible.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Base oil and FX inflation is expected to spill into Q3, and the 21%-24% margin band could be tested after Q2 EBITDA margin of ~26% helped by inventory benefit.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Company is building capabilities in specialised EV fluids and data-centre cooling fluids, but data-centre business is not yet material and no launch date was given.

rows.label: Further price action if base oil or FX moves adversely
rows.why: Two price rises in low double digits were taken in Jan-Jun 2026, and management will take further pricing if Group III base oil or FX move adversely, while competitors took about 4 increases between March and July 2026.

rows.label: Open offer tied to BP/Stonepeak Castrol global divestment
rows.why: The deal is multi-country and large, and open offer timing depends on deal closure with no timeline given.

rows.label: Interim dividend INR6.25 per share
rows.why: Interim dividend of INR6.25 per share declared, with H1 PAT of INR590 crore; past payout reportedly 80%-90%, though management did not confirm it as policy.

tone.note: Management was confident on the broad-based growth and the Q2 result, but cautious on Q3 cost inflation from base oil and FX; analysts pressed on volume split, inventory gain, the open offer timeline and whether pricing covers Q3 costs.

500870|2026-09.headline: Castrol India Q3 CY26 revenue rose 27% YoY to INR 1,735 crore, but EBITDA fell 19% to INR 262 crore (~15% margin) on raw material inflation.
500870|2026-09.overview: Q3 revenue from operations was INR 1,735 crore, up 27% YoY but down 7% QoQ, while EBITDA fell 19% YoY to INR 262 crore and PAT fell 23% YoY to INR 176 crore. Management attributed the squeeze to a sharp rise in commodity and raw material costs (cited as a 60-plus percent increase in the raw material bill) and adverse currency moves, partly offset by early-year pricing actions. Over nine months, revenue grew 20% to INR 5,151 crore, EBITDA rose 11% to INR 1,086 crore and PAT rose 9% to INR 766 crore. Management declined to give forward quarterly guidance and said margins will sit outside the 21-24% EBITDA band in the short to medium term.

segments.name: Industrial lubricants
segments.commentary: Delivered another quarter of double-digit volume growth in the September quarter; added close to 400 customers net over the full year and 9 months, with growth in steel and cement and new metalworking fluid launches (Hysol 35 XBB, Hysol 61 XBB, boron-free). Management said industrial margin is healthy and above last year's level.

segments.name: Automotive / consumer and commercial vehicle
segments.commentary: No separate volume figures given. Management said Q2 and Q3 were managed together and volume growth looked healthy; company claims market share held across categories. Institutional customers include Tata, Maruti and JCB.

segments.name: Thermal management / data-centre cooling
segments.commentary: Early-stage. Two latest products certified by NVIDIA about 1.5 months before the call for direct-to-chip cooling; business is in ongoing pilots and not a substantial part of revenue or profit today.

guidance_outlook: No quarterly guidance given; management cited unprecedented raw material volatility.
Medium-term EBITDA margin expected to fall outside the 21-24% band in the short to medium term; the 21-24% band remains the target over time.
Management said it will operate within a 21-24% EBITDA frame over the medium term while growing volume at least 1.5x to 2x the market growth rate.
Plant utilisation expected to stay in the 70-80% range through the year.
Market growth in India estimated at 3-4% in a normal year; this year may see headwinds, with Castrol tracking ahead.
Capex historically INR 100-150 crore per year, focused on plant innovation, capacity and consumer/trade visibility.

Stonepeak acquisition of Castrol from BP: completion targeted by end CY26 per the deal; management said licence work across 50+ countries is progressing well, with SEBI disclosure to follow on completion.
capex_capacity: Plants run at around 70-80% utilisation; expected to remain in the same range through the year, with seasonal flex.
Historical capex of INR 100-150 crore per year; no specific CY27 capex figure given.
Localisation of inputs and reformulation are being used to reduce bill of materials and cash cost.
Supply-chain efficiency work under way for 6-7 months to partly offset raw material inflation.
demand_pricing: Raw material bill up 60-plus percent in Q3; COGS as a percentage of sales up 61% YoY.
Pricing actions taken early in the year; further pricing to be taken as and when required, calibrated by sector, with no forward guidance.
About 40% of business is B2B; some B2B contracts have price-flex clauses for input-cost pass-through, while B2C pricing varies by channel.
Base oil prices: Base Oil 2 down about 5% and Base Oil 3 down about 7% in Q3 per an analyst; management said the cost environment remains substantially challenged versus last year.
Crude oil went from about $120 in Q2 to about $80, and is now back at $114-115 per management.

Network of about 167,000 outlets, including 46,000 in rural small-town India; Auto Care in 50,000 stores; about 870 Castrol Auto Service centres, 37,000 independent bike workshops and 16,000 multi-brand workshops; Rural Service Express at over 1,000 locations.

qa_highlights.question: What is the volume guidance and how is pricing balanced against market share?
qa_highlights.answer: Management gave no guidance for the next few months given the unprecedented raw material moves; it reiterated the aim to gain volume and share, with pricing balanced to let consumers move to new price points.

qa_highlights.question: What are the capex and margin guidance for CY27, and hedging plans?
qa_highlights.answer: Capex historically INR 100-150 crore; investments prioritise growth drivers. Margin protection is to come from a mix of pricing and cost prudence; no hedging detail was given.

qa_highlights.question: Status of the Stonepeak acquisition and the DPS filing in India?
qa_highlights.answer: Licence work across more than 50 countries is progressing well; SEBI will be informed on completion, with no timeline beyond that.

qa_highlights.question: Is Castrol refocusing on the OEM business?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not call out OEM as a separate focus; it said it works with OEMs such as Tata, Maruti and JCB on new engine platform technology.

qa_highlights.question: Segment-wise sales and Q3 volume trend?
qa_highlights.answer: Volume growth ahead of market over nine months; industrial grew double digits in Q3; automotive volumes were described as healthy across Q2 and Q3 combined, with no specific figures.

qa_highlights.question: What is the reference margin per litre, and does lower absolute EBITDA imply lower volumes?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said per-litre EBITDA is an internal frame, and the external measure is percentage margin: 26% in Q2, 15% in Q3, 21% over six and nine months.

qa_highlights.question: Are plants and margins expected to recover, and what levers are there?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the 21-24% band will be reached only once volatility subsides, with levers in supplier diversification, localisation, reformulation and supply-chain efficiency.

qa_highlights.question: Data-centre cooling: size of opportunity and how sales are routed?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said products are globally approved and sold through Castrol India, with NVIDIA certification as a base requirement; it declined to size the opportunity, saying it is not yet material.

risks_watch: Raw material and crude/FX volatility: margin per litre is the stated measure, but guidance has been withdrawn.
Q4 CY26 margin and volume recovery; watch pricing action and base oil rebates in Oct-Dec.
Volume softness in the short to medium term given market headwinds.
Stonepeak-BP transaction: completion by end CY26 and any change to the timeline.
Limited disclosure: analysts pressed for segment and volume detail, and an analyst asked for more specific guidance.

500877|2026-03.headline: Apollo Tyres Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue rose about 14% to INR 73.4 bn with 14.6% EBITDA margin, while India and Europe face a steep raw-material cost push.
500877|2026-03.overview: Consolidated revenue grew about 14% YoY to INR 73.4 bn and EBITDA margin was 14.6% versus 13% a year ago, despite roughly INR 100 crore of extra cricket-jersey sponsorship and activation spend. India revenue rose 14.3% to INR 52.4 bn on high-teens volume growth in both replacement and OE, with a 14.6% margin. Europe revenue fell 1% to EUR 170 mn, with EBITDA of EUR 25 mn (14.6% margin), and the Enschede plant closure carried a EUR 43 mn non-cash write-off. Management guided to a sharp raw-material cost increase (mid to high teens QoQ in Q1) and is taking two rounds of price hikes totalling 6-8%, with more needed.

financial_highlights.change: +14% YoY, c.+2% QoQ implied by India commentary
-1% YoY (c.-3% incl. other operating income drop)
from 0.7x at March 2025 and about 3x in March 2020 per management

financial_highlights.metric: Deferred tax benefit from concessional regime
financial_highlights.value: c.INR 570 crore+ positive net impact in P&L
financial_highlights.change: tax rate India cut from 34% to 25% from FY27

segments.name: India Operations
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 52.4 bn (+14.3% YoY), EBITDA INR 7.6 bn at 14.6% margin; high-teens volume growth in OE and replacement, TBR replacement up 20%+ and PCR replacement single-digit OE/high-single to 20%+ per management split. Capacity utilisation about 90%.

segments.name: Europe Operations
segments.commentary: Revenue EUR 170 mn (-1% YoY) on muted market; passenger car outperformed market while truck supply was hit by India supply issues. EBITDA EUR 25 mn at 14.6% margin vs 14.3%.

guidance_outlook: Raw material costs expected to rise mid to high teens sequentially in Q1 FY27; Q2 could be marginally higher than Q1 if current levels persist.
Price hikes of 6-8% announced for Q1 FY27 in India (3-5% implemented, rest in May); at least two more rounds needed beyond this to offset cost push.
India margins to remain under pressure in near term; management expects margin normalisation with pricing catch-up over time.
A&P spend to normalise at around 2.5% plus of sales from 4% in Q4 FY26 (typical 2%).
Enschede plant last production day June 30, 2026; positive European margin impact expected from H2 FY27.
FY27 consolidated capex of INR 35 bn, about 80% growth/capacity; roughly INR 3,000 crore India, balance Europe (mainly Hungary passenger car expansion).
Europe cash outflow of about EUR 50 mn in FY27 for social plan; total cash provision of EUR 55 mn-plus already taken.
Europe blended tax rate about 20%; India 25% from FY27.
capex_capacity: FY27 capex outlined at INR 35 bn, with nearly 80% towards growth and capacity expansion.
India capex close to INR 3,000 crore of the INR 3,500 crore (per transcript figures) covering truck and car tyre capacity expansion.
Hungary plant: passenger car tyre expansion already well underway; no truck expansion there.
Capacity utilisation at about 90% across India and Europe; management expects full utilisation and continues planned expansion.
Management said FY27 is largely committed for the previously announced large capex plan; some flexibility exists for FY28 if demand slows.
Export volumes to be deprioritised in favour of home markets India and Europe given tight capacity, especially in truck tyres.
demand_pricing: India volume growth high teens YoY in both OE and replacement in Q4; sequential volume growth about 2% QoQ, which accounted for all of the 2% QoQ revenue growth.
Standalone exports up mid-single digits in Q4; US market weak, though price increases of mid to high single digits announced there.
Market share: management believes it gained share in TBR replacement for FY26 and in PCR replacement, but not in PCR OE; based on internal estimates.
Dealer inventory in India: no marked difference in levels.

Raw material costs: natural rubber INR 200/kg in Q4 rising to INR 250/kg currently; synthetic rubber INR 170, carbon black INR 110, steel cord INR 155 per kg in Q4. Blended RM basket up about 1% QoQ in Q4.
OEM contracts largely follow a formula with a three-month lag; some OEMs negotiated with only small increases so far.
Competition: all peers have announced price hikes, with Apollo and CEAT slightly ahead; management does not expect discounting-led aggressive pricing near term.
Europe: 2% price increase announced; Apollo is a price follower and waiting for competitors. Europe needs less than half the price increase India needs for the same raw-material rise.
Management expects April demand to be as strong as Q4, but second-half FY27 is uncertain given GDP downgrades and fuel/tyre inflation; new vehicle purchases likely to be deferred first.

qa_highlights.question: Why are Europe margins still well below pre-crisis levels, and what drove the restructuring?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Europe margins were 16%+ historically but now 14-15% because of two years of flat to negative market, high energy costs and Dutch salary inflation of 12-13% a year versus a usual 4-5%. That led to the Enschede closure decision.

qa_highlights.question: Will Q2 commodity costs rise further and how much more price is needed?
qa_highlights.answer: Current RM inflation is mid to high teens. About half of the needed price increase has been taken, so at least a couple more rounds are needed. If spot levels hold, Q2 could be marginally higher than Q1.

qa_highlights.question: How much Europe revenue is at risk from the Enschede closure?

Growth is coming through debottlenecking, replacing lower-capacity extruders with higher-capacity ones, rather than large greenfield or brownfield projects.
Capex outlay remains INR125-200 crore, unchanged.

Ratnagiri PVC: EDC-based line running without interruption. VCM-based line does not run during the June-September monsoon months because the Ratnagiri jetty is fair-weather only. VCM availability is constrained by Middle East force majeure and Northeast Asia feedstock constraints.
CPVC extrusion capacity is considered sufficient for near-term CPVC growth, according to management.
demand_pricing: Average PVC price in Q1 was about USD875/MT versus USD707/MT a year earlier (ICIS), carried over from elevated Q4 FY26 levels. A sharp intra-quarter correction in April triggered channel destocking.
Management cited INR96 to INR92 to INR82/kg as the PVC price path through April. Analyst cited a INR12-13/kg hike in the last 15-20 days after the MIP and duty changes.
Customs duty exemption on PVC resin was withdrawn in mid-July, and a minimum import price (MIP) was imposed. Management said these should support price stability and channel inventory.
Pass-through: management said almost all of the recent price increase (barring INR1-2) has been passed to customers.
Demand: July was the best month of the four, with a strong pickup; August to date was described as moving in the right direction.
Channel inventory is near normal, with some room left. A lot of stocking occurred in July in anticipation of price increases. Quantification in days was not given.
PVC-EDC spread was ~USD501/MT in Q1 FY27 versus ~USD522 a year earlier, and ~USD490 currently. PVC-VCM spread was INR122/kg in Q1 FY27 versus INR163 a year earlier.
Pricing: management said Finolex prices ~10-12% above Supreme-type peers in the market (ballpark only).
Market share: management said FY26 share of the top 5-6 reporting companies was about 22%, and it sees no change in Q1. An analyst cited FY23 share of about 27%.
JJM 2.0: management said the outlay is about INR67,000 crore, not higher than JJM 1.0. All sales go through channel partners, so there is no direct correlation to volume.

qa_highlights.question: Why did realization not rise QoQ when peers reported 7-9% jumps?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said realization per kg was up ~15% vs the same quarter last year and was in line with peers. It said Q4 FY26 was an aberration with a sharp price rise, and that falling PVC prices in April drove the QoQ result. Discounts and incentives also affect net realization.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the volume decline was agri vs non-agri, and what were the monthly trends?

qa_highlights.question: What drove the margin expansion despite falling volumes?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the margin was largely top-line driven, with costs range-bound. It cited backward integration and the timing of raw material procurement as a cushion. It did not quantify inventory gains or losses.

qa_highlights.question: Will full-year volume decline? Can H1 be flat YoY?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to guide full-year volume. It said July was a good month and that flattish H1 YoY is possible, with a plus if July's pace holds, while August and September are still to be seen.

qa_highlights.question: Why not deploy the INR2,636 crore cash into CPVC capacity and shareholder returns?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said CPVC extrusion capacity is sufficient and CPVC is about 7-8% of the PVC pipe market, which Finolex matches. It said the Board decides on cash deployment or returns and will announce when a decision is made.

qa_highlights.question: Why is margin guidance sub-15% when Q1 delivered 12%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is holding the sub-15% guidance from Q4 because of volatility in Q1 and wants another quarter of data before revising it.

qa_highlights.question: What is the VCM supply situation and the PVC plant utilization outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: VCM availability is limited by Middle East force majeure and Northeast Asia feedstock constraints. The VCM line does not run during monsoon months (about June to September) because of the fair-weather jetty. Management said efforts to secure supply are ongoing and H2 is uncertain.

500940|2026-09.headline: Finolex Industries Q2 FY27 volume rose 28% YoY to 83,407 MT, but PBT was flat at INR153 crore as raw material cost lag squeezed margins.

PBT was roughly flat at INR153 crore versus INR158 crore a year earlier, as higher-cost inventory consumed in Q2 lagged the rise in PVC prices. H1 volume fell 4% YoY to 151,106 MT and H1 revenue rose 4% to INR1,978 crore. Management guided full-year EBITDA of about INR15/kg (roughly 14-15%) and said October was a good month.

Q2 margin pressure attributed to a lag in raw material cost: inventory bought at lower prices in Q1 was consumed in Q2 while selling prices reset immediately.

qa_highlights.question: What is full-year volume and margin outlook?

qa_highlights.question: Why is revenue growth equal to volume growth despite higher PVC prices?

qa_highlights.answer: Capex about INR150 crore planned for FY27; Board has made no decision on use or reward for cash, which stays invested at about 7.5-8% yield, with no timeline.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for agri demand given El Nino?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said El Nino impact expected from November; water-led pipe demand may rise but farmer income may be constrained, offset by strong tractor and rural two-wheeler bookings.

qa_highlights.question: Supply chain impact from Middle East disruption?

501423|2026-03.headline: Shaily FY26 revenue rose 26% to INR991 crores and PAT 83% to INR170 crores, led by Healthcare revenue up 139% to INR393 crores.
501423|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue grew 9% YoY to INR237 crores with EBITDA margin of 29.3% and PAT of INR40 crores (up 40%). Healthcare doubled in Q4 to INR113 crores on Semaglutide pen injector commercial launches in Canada and India, while Consumer fell 31% to INR102 crores on weak US and European home furnishing demand. Management announced a semiconductor tray supply agreement and first commercial supplies to a consumer electronics customer, and an INR500 crore enabling fundraise resolution (described as annual, with no specific raise planned). The pen capacity ramp is behind plan: the 25 million-unit line added in March runs at about 45% efficiency.

qa_highlights.answer: No. It is an annual enabling resolution for flexibility; no capital is being raised now, and any future need would be a one-off large capex for device capacity outside India and Abu Dhabi.

501423|2026-09.headline: Q2 FY27 revenue hit a record INR320 crores (+24% YoY) and EBITDA crossed INR100 crores for the first time at a 31.9% margin, led by Healthcare (+78% YoY).

Healthcare became the largest segment at 55% of revenue, while Consumer stayed about 14% below last year and was flat QoQ, which management called stabilisation. Management said West Asia freight and polymer costs and weak European and US home-furnishing demand shaped the quarter, and it prioritised margin over Consumer volume. Management also said the 25 million pen capacity starts qualification next week and could sell from December.

capex_capacity: GEML invested INR331 crores via rights issue (total INR530 crore issue, fully subscribed by GCL and Abdul Latif Jameel in proportion to holding).
GEML 2-wheeler production capacity is about 480,000 units.
Robotic gantry cell commissioned at CSN facility; Excel debottlenecking added 10-15% output; Excel pushpull cable utilisation at 70-75%, rubber line just starting.
Pilot Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) facility commissioned; commercial launch targeted in subsequent quarters.
Core business capex stated as on track; 650 kVA own engine launched last quarter.
demand_pricing: GEML 2-wheeler run rate roughly 9,000-10,000 units in the latest quarter; growing ~2,000 units per quarter.
Raw material price indexing for OEM contracts applies with a lag; aftermarket pricing passed through via distributors.

Strong demand for medium-horsepower gensets in industrial and commercial applications; AI data-centre demand described as strong, with a strategic supply agreement with a large global engine maker for larger sizes.
Excel: business restarted from Europe and expected from the US after a Russia-Ukraine-related export setback last year.
International business is about 13% of core revenue; Greaves International Trading FZE set up in Dubai for Middle East and Africa.

qa_highlights.question: How has margin erosion split between OEM and aftermarket/retail?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said commodity costs hit all products. OEM contracts have indexing with a lag, while aftermarket pricing is easier to pass on; price increases have been taken in both.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the margin drop is investment versus commodity cost?
qa_highlights.answer: Manish Poddar attributed about 1.5 percentage points to additional investments; the rest is the inflation-price lag, which should narrow in Q2 and fully in Q3.

qa_highlights.question: Is GEML's growth sustainable and when does it turn EBITDA-positive?
qa_highlights.answer: Vikas Singh said per-unit losses have fallen sharply and EBITDA could turn positive in 4 to 6 quarters, without committing to timing or scale.

qa_highlights.question: Why does GFL, an EV financing NBFC, exist in a pruned portfolio, and is it brand-agnostic?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said GFL is part of the EV ecosystem; its share of GEML financing is near double digits and rising. Vikas Singh said financing partners are brand-agnostic by nature.

qa_highlights.question: Is there enough cash for the investee investments?
qa_highlights.answer: Manish Poddar said standalone liquidity as of March 2026 covers the INR50 crore GFL and INR331 crore GEML investments plus Q1-Q2 capex and dividends, and that the core business generates enough cash.

qa_highlights.question: Is motorcycle entry planned for GEML?
qa_highlights.answer: Vikas Singh said motorcycle prototypes are underway; the scooter opportunity is also large and prioritisation is under leadership review with no timing decided.

risks_watch: Margins: Q1 margin down 2-2.5 pts; recovery depends on Q2-H2 pricing and cost savings, and the full-year target is contingent on H2 catch-up.
Commodity and geopolitical cost pressure (West Asia developments) may outlast the pricing actions.
GEML is still loss-making with a 4-6 quarter timeline to positive EBITDA; management gave no firm timing.
Excel revenue of about INR66-70 crores and export-led recovery depend on new Europe and US customers.
Greaves Technologies had earlier slippages; management said it is still stabilising and cited one pilot design-work order.
Unallocable expenses of INR25.82 crores in segment results; the company said these are now folded into core business P&L (slide 27).
key_quotes: Now our ability to mitigate those differs slightly by the segment of customers.
And to sum it up, we're absolutely on track with our commitment to Greaves.Next strategy and the margin targets that we have set for ourselves.
We're not in a position really to comment in terms of how soon and how much, but we are very confident and that's what the entire team is working towards.
At this stage, I don't want to reveal more detail because the discussions are still evolving.

501455|2026-09.headline: Greaves Cotton Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 44% YoY to INR1,176 crore, but Core EBITDA margin fell to 11.5% from 14.8% on input-cost pressure.
501455|2026-09.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 44% YoY to INR1,176 crore in Q2 FY27 and 38% to INR2,150 crore in H1, with Core Businesses up 24% in Q2. Consolidated EBITDA margin improved marginally to 6.2% from 5.8% in Q1, but Core EBITDA margin contracted to 11.5% from 14.8% a year ago as commodity inflation outpaced pricing actions. Greaves Electric Mobility (GEML) posted record volumes and revenue of INR410 crore (up 106%), with its loss narrowing to INR25 crore from INR42 crore, and Excel Controlinkage became wholly owned after the 20% stake buyout. Q2 also carried INR60.1 crore of one-off charges (INR27.3 crore accelerated depreciation and INR32.8 crore exceptional items), which management says completes the write-off exercise.

narrowed from INR42 crore a year ago

segments.commentary: Grew 36% YoY in Q2 (vs 21% in Q1); medium horsepower genset portfolio (160-750 kVA) grew 35% in H1 vs 28% for the segment. First batch of enhanced gensets shipped to a Middle East market.

segments.name: Mobility Solutions - Automotive Engines
segments.commentary: Grew 37% YoY in Q2, driven by three-wheeler and four-wheeler demand; launched a new 470 cc diesel engine for three-wheelers.

segments.name: Mobility Solutions - Engineered Components (Excel Controlinkage)
segments.commentary: Grew 30% YoY in Q2 on new product orders and customer wins; acquired the remaining 20% stake for INR112 crore, making it wholly owned. Overall Mobility Solutions grew 23% YoY in Q2 vs 18% in Q1.

segments.name: Industrial Solutions
segments.commentary: Reported revenue broadly flat YoY in Q2 due to exit from farm equipment; 9% like-for-like growth. Launched a 750 HP fire fighting engine and unveiled a 160 cc gasoline engine prototype.

segments.name: Greaves Electric Mobility (GEML)
segments.commentary: E-two-wheeler volumes above 37,000 units (+114% YoY); L5 three-wheeler about 2,800 units (+61%). Two-wheeler revenue INR350 crore (+134%); realisation up INR5,000 to about INR93,000 per unit; EBITDA loss per unit down about 70% to under INR6,300; EBITDA margin about -7% vs -24% a year ago.

guidance_outlook: Management says profitability is the key H2 priority; margin improvement has been slower than anticipated because commodity costs keep rising.
Steady-state EBITDA margin target of 13-15% from GREAVES.NEXT is reiterated on a mid-to-long-term basis; CFO expects H2 margins to be better than H1.
Automotive price pass-through via indexed multi-year contracts starts from Q4 FY27; Energy and Industrial price increases (enacted end-Q1) expected to flow through in Q3 and Q4.
Company-wide pricing benefit expected to be fully reflected by Q4 FY27.

GEML e-two-wheeler market share 4.8% in H1 FY27 vs 4.1% in H1 FY26; top two in Tamil Nadu (about 15%) and number one in Bihar (about 18%).
Management says the company is raising prices in GEML parts; GEML realisation rose INR5,000 to about INR93,000 per unit, with IoT and accessories adding higher-margin revenue.
Core commodity pressure cited on aluminium, iron, copper, and platinum group metals used in engines and gensets.

Automotive exports described as flat in H1 (not declining); domestic three-wheeler and heavy commercial vehicle demand grew faster. A French OEM is the largest engine export customer, with some further engine discussions at advanced stages.
Fire fighting engines: management is in advanced discussions with global customers after obtaining FM/UL certification, which few peers hold.

qa_highlights.question: What are the top commodity pressures and what is steady-state gross margin?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO named aluminium, iron, copper and PGM as the main cost buckets for engines and gensets. He reiterated the 13-15% EBITDA margin steady-state target and said H2 should be better than H1.

qa_highlights.question: Are the e-two-wheeler loss-per-unit gains sustainable, or are there abnormal items?
qa_highlights.answer: Vikas Singh said loss per unit has been falling sharply quarter on quarter through pricing, product and market-penetration strategy, and expects that trajectory to continue barring force majeure.

qa_highlights.question: Why is GEML not pushing harder on sales given industry supply shortage and low utilisation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said demand exceeds supply and capacity expansion is needed; the constraint is the partner ecosystem, with no forward volume or capacity numbers given.

qa_highlights.question: Has the write-off and portfolio-review exercise finished?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said all key portfolio decisions are taken, Q2 accelerated depreciation and exceptional items (INR60.1 crore) cover the GEML review, and nothing more is planned, though periodic reviews will continue.

qa_highlights.question: How much cash does the company have and is a GEML IPO or spin-off planned?
qa_highlights.answer: Core cash is about INR150 crore against INR40 crore debt (net INR110 crore), with AA- rating and almost nil debt. No IPO date was given; an IPO committee is evaluating timing and the spin-off question is for that committee.

qa_highlights.question: Will the 2-wheeler motor and Excel 100% ownership change the outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Vikas said the rare-earth-free motor beats the rare-earth motor on performance and costs less, and will be in production in one to two quarters. Parag said Excel is being upgraded, with 30% growth in Q2.

risks_watch: Core EBITDA margin (11.5% in Q2 vs 14.8% a year ago) depends on whether the lagged price pass-through in Q3 and Q4 offsets commodity inflation.
GEML breakeven timing is not fixed; it depends on continued volume growth and unit economics, and management declined to give a date.
GEML IPO timing and structure are undecided; an analyst's spin-off suggestion was not addressed directly.
Management said Industrial Solutions has an export opportunity in fire fighting, but no quantified order book was disclosed.
Exports in Mobility Solutions are described as flat, not growing, and the French OEM is the main engine customer.

502090|2026-03.headline: Sagar Cements guides FY27 volumes to about 7 million tonnes (FY26: 6.1 Mt) and Q4 EBITDA/tonne rose to ₹445 from ₹218.
502090|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 volumes grew 8% YoY and full-year volumes grew 11% to 6.1 million tonnes, with revenue up 20% in the quarter helped by non-trade pricing. Q4 EBITDA per tonne was ₹445 against ₹218 a year earlier, and quarterly PAT was ₹100 crore. Management flagged a fuel cost shock from the West Asia conflict (pet coke at $136-140 CIF versus about $120 earlier), with impact expected from mid-Q2 if prices do not ease. Management also announced a Superfine Building Materials division and in-principle approval for merging Andhra Cements into the parent.

segments.name: Plants (Q4 utilisation)
segments.commentary: Mattampally 59%, Gudipadu 84%, Bayyavaram 69%, Jeerabad 95%, Jajpur 44%, Dachepalli 38%. Jeerabad is cited as consistently running around 90%.

segments.name: Superfine Building Materials (new division)
segments.commentary: Approved by the board on 13 May 2026. It will use GGBS and fly ash to make superfine products (Blaine target 10,000-20,000) for UHPC, repairs and cladding. Management guides a minimum 30% margin; revenue and EBITDA numbers are deferred to next quarter.

guidance_outlook: FY27 volume target of about 7 million tonnes, relying on about 0.5 Mt from Jeerabad upgrade (expected by end-Q1), about 0.9 Mt from Andhra ramp-up and the balance from market growth of 12-15%.
FY27 EBITDA per tonne expected to be close to ₹600 if prices stay flat, with about ₹150/tonne from internal cost savings (WHRS, Andhra preheater, grinding units).

Pet coke and coal cost pressure: about ₹200/tonne at clinker and ₹100-150/tonne at cement on current blend, with impact from mid-Q2 if prices stay high. Management also pencilled in about ₹225-250/tonne in total fuel and miscellaneous cost increases, assumed to be passed through.
FY27 budget: ₹580 crore cost, about ₹100 crore lower than the prior year's cost base according to management's comments.

Capex: ₹190 crore pending on three ongoing projects (Andhra ₹140 crore, Gudipadu ₹17 crore, Jeerabad ₹33 crore). Maintenance capex about ₹50 crore per year. Some projects to be funded through lease or equipment finance.
Vizag land monetisation (about 100 acres, net about ₹3.5 crore per acre): ₹350 crore pencilled over 18-24 months, with ₹150 crore in year 1 after the government GO, and ₹150 crore assumed in FY27.
Net debt guidance for FY27 is to pay debt down from operating cash flow; year-end net debt was about ₹1,550 crore versus the earlier guidance of about ₹1,300 crore.
capex_capacity: WHRS: 2.8 MW of 4.35 MW (AQC boiler) commissioned on 12 May 2026; remaining 1.55 MW (preheater boiler) due by end-June 2026.
Jeerabad grinding expansion and Dachepalli expansion in progress; Jeerabad due before end of Q1 FY27.
Andhra Cements grinding expansion due by September 2026; new VRM for cement grinding due by September 2026.
Andhra clinker kcal consumption about 700 kcal/tonne of clinker versus about 775-780 earlier.
Madhya Pradesh incentives of about ₹171 crore over seven years; about ₹65 crore received so far, about ₹110 crore remaining over four years.
demand_pricing: Industry demand held up in the first two months of Q4 but slowed in late Q4 due to labour shortages, the festive season and unseasonal rains. Q4 volume growth was 8%, and Q1 FY27 to date is up about 7% YoY.
Price hike of about ₹25-30 per bag in second week of April (non-trade led) across regions; Hyderabad retail about ₹295 and wholesale about ₹268 after the hike.
Prices have been flat since mid-April, with some pressure in central and eastern markets (₹5 hike in Indore not sustained) and a slight negative bias there; south has held the April hike.
Demand outlook: AP and Telangana strong; Tamil Nadu 5-10%, Karnataka 5%, Odisha 5%, Madhya Pradesh 5-7.5%.
Management said bags cost fell about ₹2/bag, but the war impact on explosives and diesel (₹23.75/litre hike in commercial diesel) is expected to add about ₹100/tonne.
Superfine products priced around ₹30,000/tonne versus ₹2,500-3,000/tonne for low-Blaine GGBS, with low volumes expected initially.

qa_highlights.question: What is the expected cost impact from the West Asia crisis?
qa_highlights.answer: Pet coke has risen from around $120 to $136-140 CIF, adding about ₹200/tonne at clinker and ₹100-150/tonne at cement. Inventory cover runs to mid-Q2, and imported coal is being partly switched to domestic coal, with the outcome known by end-Q1.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other expenses rise 28% QoQ?
qa_highlights.answer: Around ₹11.5 crore was one-offs: about ₹7.5 crore mine bearing land (MBL) cess and about ₹3.24 crore DMF expense at a subsidiary, covering roughly 3-3.5 years of accrual. Promotional spend also rose. Excluding one-offs, growth is about 26%.

qa_highlights.question: Can FY27 volume of 7 Mt be achieved given past misses?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the target relies on Jeerabad (+0.5 Mt), Andhra ramp-up (+0.9 Mt) and market growth; it chooses not to chase share at the expense of cash.

qa_highlights.question: Will Jeerabad clinker sales continue in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Some clinker sales are expected during the phased ramp-up, subject to clinker prices, with margin held at that location's level.

qa_highlights.question: Is there any cost reduction left after Andhra stabilised?
qa_highlights.answer: Andhra clinker cost is now in line; the new VRM (by September) should deliver the planned savings. Margins are expected to be better in FY27 than FY26.

qa_highlights.question: Why did net debt rise above guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Promoter unsecured debt for the Andhra project was drawn after the planned rights issue became an OFS, and solar capex was accelerated for short payback. Debt is expected to fall from operating cash flow.

qa_highlights.question: Working capital days rose sharply: why?
qa_highlights.answer: Credit days were extended in a difficult market, fuel prices were higher, and volumes grew. About ₹80 crore of US coal was bought in March on 180-day LC credit. Moderation is expected.

qa_highlights.question: Vizag land GO status and sale timing?
qa_highlights.answer: GVMC and UDA approvals are in place; the state GO is awaited, expected within six months. Management is assuming ₹350 crore over 18-24 months at the old reckoner rate of ₹4 crore per acre.

qa_highlights.question: Operating cost gap between standalone and Andhra?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the gap is mainly logistics and market spread, with the Andhra cost gap closing after investments; detail to be discussed offline.

risks_watch: Fuel cost inflation: pet coke and coal may add ₹100-150/tonne at cement from mid-Q2 if prices do not ease; a ₹225-250/tonne total cost pass-through is assumed.
Pricing: the April hike is holding in the south, but central and eastern prices are flat to slightly negative.
Execution: Jeerabad upgrade (0.5 Mt), Andhra ramp-up (0.9 Mt), WHRS completion by end-June and VRM by September; past volume guidance has been missed.
Debt and working capital: year-end net debt about ₹1,550 crore, above prior guidance; working capital elevated; funding of ₹190 crore capex needs lease finance.
Vizag land monetisation depends on the state GO, which is still awaited; ₹150 crore is pencilled into FY27.
Incentive receipts: about ₹23 crore outstanding at March 2026, expected mid-July 2026.

502090|2026-06.headline: Sagar Cements Q1 FY27: volumes up ~13% YoY but loss after tax of ₹28 crore and EBITDA of ₹451/tonne on West Asia-driven cost inflation.
502090|2026-06.overview: Volumes grew about 13% YoY and revenue rose 5% YoY, with realisations broadly stable. Profitability moderated as energy, fuel and packaging costs rose amid West Asia tensions, leaving EBITDA at ₹451 per tonne and a loss after tax of ₹28 crore. Management maintained a 7 million tonne volume target for FY27 (excluding clinker) and reiterated FY27 EBITDA guidance of ₹500–550 per tonne, down from the earlier ~₹600 reference raised by an analyst. Capex completed in the quarter includes Jeerabad 0.5 million tonne expansion and the remaining 1.55 MW of Gudipadu waste heat recovery; the 0.75 million tonne Andhra Cements expansion is expected by quarter-end.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 7 million tonne FY27 volume target ex-clinker, and how much clinker will be sold in Q2 and beyond?
qa_highlights.answer: The 7 mt target excludes clinker. Clinker is still sold to Andhra Cements' sister unit Bayyavaram and some outside, and some at Jeerabad until ramp-up; management would not quantify volumes.

qa_highlights.question: Is double-digit volume growth possible in FY28, and what is the Q2 cost inflation and is the ~₹600/t EBITDA guidance intact?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says FY27 and FY28 both see double-digit volume growth. Full-year cost pressure is about ₹100/t across fuel, raw material and miscellaneous, offset by savings; Q2 gets extra inventory and maintenance cost at three plants. Guidance is ₹500–550/t, assuming flat prices, not ~₹600.

qa_highlights.question: Are prices stable versus Q1 averages?
qa_highlights.answer: Prices have been flat from March exit to July and June to July; realisation was up about ₹50–60/t, with the cause unclear (mix or price hikes).

qa_highlights.question: Status of Vizag land sale and FY27 realisation?
qa_highlights.answer: Awaiting a generic Government GO after the government signalled it would replace a case-specific order; the ₹150 crore for FY27 is still seen as doable. Management said buyer engagement exists but timelines were the issue.

qa_highlights.question: Which regions drive incremental H2 FY27 demand?
qa_highlights.answer: Almost all incremental volume comes from the South (~80% of footprint). Madpradesh is also expected to rise after the 0.5 mt Jeerabad expansion, supporting the ~15% growth projected for the year.

qa_highlights.question: How does Andhra Cements' cost structure compare with Mattampally, and how should the three units be modelled?
qa_highlights.answer: Variable cost at Andhra is ₹100–125/t higher than Mattampally because it buys grid power without waste heat recovery; management says the kcal and unit metrics are at par. Andhra carries most of the debt, and management offered to share modelling details offline.

qa_highlights.question: Can Q1 EBITDA of ~₹425/t reach ₹600/t for full year?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said ₹550/t is 'definitely doable', citing Gudipadu WHR savings, Jeerabad expansion and the Andhra cement mill due end-September, assuming stable prices.

qa_highlights.question: Is capex going to rise, and what is the debt reduction path?
qa_highlights.answer: No new capex beyond ₹30–40 crore annual maintenance through 2028. About ₹240 crore of ongoing capex spreads over FY27 and FY28; operating cash flow is not yet reflected in the gross debt path.

qa_highlights.question: What are the levers to manage power and fuel costs if the West Asia crisis escalates?
qa_highlights.answer: Management has no control over prices and can only manage consumption, which it says is efficient. Inventory covers operations to mid-October; ₹100/t inflation is pencilled in (₹50 fuel, ₹50 other), and clinker is at its peak.

qa_highlights.question: What is the impact of the Tamil Nadu ban on rough stone and aggregate transport, and what limestone auction premiums are seen?
qa_highlights.answer: Management sees no impact. Recent Telangana limestone auctions, about a year or 18 months old, went at 50–75% premiums; other auctions are pending in TN, AP and Telangana.

qa_highlights.question: Will the land sale and volume ramp support the net debt projection?
qa_highlights.answer: Parth Bhavsar asked about net debt trajectory. Management said the ₹150 crore land sale is in FY27 and about ₹200 crore in FY28.

502090|2026-09.headline: Sagar Cements Q2 FY27 volumes rose 26% YoY, but loss after tax of ₹52 crore; management guides FY27 EBITDA of ₹350-375 crore.

Management said the company has hit its margin bottom and expects H2 recovery driven by South price hikes of about ₹25 per bag on average (roughly ₹500 per ton realisation uplift). FY27 EBITDA guidance was revised to ₹350-375 crore (about ₹525 per ton) from the earlier ~₹410 crore projection. Net debt has peaked with CapEx largely complete and is expected to decline from Q4 FY27.

502219|2026-03.headline: Borosil Renewables FY26 standalone sales rose 38% to INR1,534.83 crore and EBITDA margin hit 32% on higher solar glass realisations.
502219|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 standalone sales were INR437.62 crore (up ~34% YoY, a record quarter) with EBITDA of INR144.61 crore at 33% of sales, helped by average ex-factory realisation of INR150.2/mm and about 15% higher volumes. Management attributed roughly half the quarterly sales jump to Ind AS revenue recognition timing (about 6% of Q4 sales), and said the run-rate is nearer INR400-410 crore a quarter. Fuel surcharges passed to customers during the West Asia-driven gas price spike had negligible net impact on realisation (under INR1/mm). The company wrote off its German exposure (Geosphere and GMB) with no additional P&L loss, as a provision was already made in Q1 FY26. Management also announced a rooftop solar branded-products venture, a 600 TPD furnace expansion targeted for Q4 FY27, and an enabling resolution to raise up to INR750 crore in equity.

segments.commentary: FY26 sales INR1,534.83 crore with EBITDA margin 32%; Q4 volumes up 15% YoY and 14% QoQ, with production run at full capacity and no curtailment during the West Asia disruption.

segments.commentary: Q4 FY26 overseas net revenue INR2.3 crore and EBITDA INR0.82 crore, versus INR3.96 crore and INR1.90 crore in the prior quarter; German production shut from July 2025 and exposure to Geosphere and GMB written off.

Management cited INR950 crore of capitalisation planned in the current financial year.

Domestic solar glass capacity is about 2,600 TPD (about 18 GW); about 33 GW of further capacity is expected by March 2027, mostly captive, taking the domestic total to about 51 GW against demand of about 65 GW.
Rooftop business: no capex for 1-1.5 years; the company may consider inverter assembly after 6-8 months to a year, but not module manufacturing.
Board approved an enabling resolution to raise equity up to INR750 crore, subject to shareholder approval; management said there are no current plans to raise capital.
demand_pricing: Realisation held near INR150/mm; management said pass-through of gas and fuel cost added less than INR1/mm, and that the price is tied to the landed cost of Chinese imports and near peak levels, with rupee depreciation providing only limited headroom.
Domestic solar installations were 44.6 GW in FY26 versus 23.8 GW in FY25, implying about 60-62 GW of glass consumption; imports still supply about 70% of demand.
ALMM-II (domestic solar cells) effective June 2026; solar cell capacity at 30 GW, expected to reach 75 GW by FY-end; ALMM-III for ingots and wafers from June 2028.

Indonesian Chinese-owned plant (about 1,500 TPD) has entered the market but has made limited impact so far; the Turkish producer's exports face high freight costs; the UAE plant is blocked by Strait of Hormuz conditions.
Export demand is low in major markets; the US may grow as customers seek non-Chinese origin glass, and Europe has niche demand for greenhouses and flat-plate collectors.

Cost pressure from oil-linked inputs is so far modest; vendors are seeking pass-through and the company is negotiating; gas quantities are secured under medium- and short-term contracts, but spot prices are high.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the INR150/mm realisation comes from fuel pass-through, and what would it be without it?
qa_highlights.answer: Ashok Jain said the pass-through contributed less than INR1/mm, about INR0.70-0.75, and a similar increase is visible in net realisation between Q3 and Q4.

qa_highlights.question: Will realisation or margins come under pressure as new domestic capacity arrives?
qa_highlights.answer: Management sees no pressure for domestic producers; most upcoming capacity is captive, demand exceeds the 51 GW expected capacity, and Indonesian imports are not yet a price threat.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the 13-15% sequential sales growth with flat realisation?
qa_highlights.answer: Roughly half was production gain (about 7%) and half was Ind AS timing: in-transit sales were lower at the end of Q3 and so were recognised in Q4, with the sales base reset to about INR400-410 crore a quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Is gas supply secure given the West Asia crisis?
qa_highlights.answer: Quantities are broadly secured under medium- and short-term contracts; the government gas cut is based on the past six-month average, and the rest is bought at market-related prices, so price rather than volume is the constraint.

qa_highlights.question: What is the rooftop solar roadmap, capex and margin profile?

qa_highlights.question: Will the furnace expansion commissioning timeline hold, and what does it do to margins?

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for depreciation and tax?
qa_highlights.answer: Depreciation has fallen because older SG1 and SG2 assets are fully depreciated; current charge mainly reflects the 2023 expansion. Tax is around 21% of PBT, with deferred tax at a similar rate.

502219|2026-09.headline: Borosil Renewables Q2 FY27 solar glass sales were INR382.1 crore with EBITDA margin down to 30.4% on furnace maintenance and a 2.8% price cut, with October output reported higher.

502355|2026-03.overview: Balkrishna posted its highest-ever quarterly and annual OHT volumes, with Q4 volume up 5% YoY to 85,820 MT and FY26 volume at 317,356 MT. Standalone Q4 revenue rose 2% YoY to INR2,894 crore, but EBITDA margin was hit late in the quarter by geopolitical supply-chain headwinds, and FY26 EBITDA fell 10% YoY to INR2,423 crore. The company has stopped giving volume guidance, is starting its on-highway push (TBR, 2-wheeler, PCR), and has approved an additional INR2,000 crore capex. Management signalled raw material and margin pressure into FY27 with only partial price pass-through so far.

segments.name: Off-highway tyres (OHT)
segments.commentary: Q4 volume of 85,820 MT (+5% YoY) was a record; H2 clearly stronger than H1 with Europe recovering on easing channel inventories and Americas improving. US was just under 10% of FY26 volume, with a target of about 10% in FY27.

segments.name: Carbon black
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue grew marginally; third-party sales were about 9% of the business. Capacity is 265,000 MTPA after the December 2025 line, with the new lines fully utilised; about 30% of output is consumed internally and about 70% sold externally at industry-average margins.

segments.name: On-highway tyres (OHT-on-road)
segments.commentary: Entered truck-bus radial with launches in February 2026 and re-launched 2-wheeler tyres (capacity about 100,000 tyres a month). Phase 1 CV radial capex of INR750 crore added 800 tyres a day of fungible CVR/OHT capacity; PCR launch is targeted by end of calendar 2026 with first-phase capacity of 6,700 tyres a day. Long-term vision is INR5,000 crore revenue by 2030.

guidance_outlook: No volume guidance for FY27 given the geopolitical uncertainty; management expects growth but declined to quantify it.
Raw material prices rose about 4-5% in Q4 FY26 and are expected to rise a further 7-8% in the June 2026 quarter.
Price hikes of 3-5% already taken across geographies, with a further roughly 2% targeted by end of May 2026; more hikes possible.

Management aims to sustain EBITDA margins of 23-25% at company level even as on-highway scales up; 5-year revenue growth vision of about 17% CAGR, with the jump back-ended as capacity comes on line.
EUR/INR realization about INR99 in Q4; FY27 hedge rate expected to be higher than this year, not yet quantified.
Final dividend of INR4 per share recommended, on top of INR12 paid over the previous three quarters.
risks_watch: Raw material inflation of 7-8% in the June 2026 quarter, with only partial pass-through through price hikes; management flagged likely near-term margin pressure in FY27.
Geopolitical supply-chain disruption affecting freight (about 4.5-5% of revenue) and margins.
Execution risk on the on-highway ramp (TBR, PCR, 2-wheeler) with no disclosed revenue targets for FY27 and PCR launch slated for end-2026.

qa_highlights.answer: Management stopped volume guidance due to geopolitical uncertainty; expects growth but will not quantify. CV radial business has just begun, with the 2030 vision still the target.

qa_highlights.question: Total FY27 capex and the INR2,000 crore additional capex: what it covers and whether it is incremental to the INR6,800 crore plan?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 capex guided at INR1,500-1,800 crore. The INR2,000 crore covers capacity expansion, infrastructure, AI automation and sustainability, staggered over several years. qa_highlights.answer: Management said the company as a whole aims to keep sustained EBITDA levels, which it is maintaining; the 23-25% range is the endeavour, applied at company level rather than by segment.

502355|2026-06.headline: Balkrishna Q1 FY27 OHT volume rose 16% YoY to 93,770 MT, but standalone EBITDA margin fell to 20.61% on raw-material inflation.
502355|2026-06.overview: Management reported record OHT sales volume of 93,770 MT (up 16% YoY) and standalone revenue of INR3,409 crores (up 24% YoY). Standalone EBITDA was INR703 crores at a 20.61% margin, pressured by raw-material costs linked to geopolitical disruption, partly offset by a ~5% price hike. PAT was INR432 crores. The On-Highway business (truck-bus radial and 2-wheeler) went live in Q1 and is being seeded, with a ramp expected from Q2; management declined to disclose its revenue or volume.

segments.name: Off-Highway Tyres (OHT)
segments.commentary: Record quarterly volume, up 16% YoY, with India at roughly 40% of volumes. Management attributed the margin dip partly to India's higher volume mix, which it said is marginally lower-margin than exports.

segments.name: On-Highway (TBR and 2-wheeler)
segments.commentary: Launched in Q1 through distributors set up in April; management calls it small and will not disclose revenue or volume. Target of INR5,000 crores On-Highway revenue by 2030 was reiterated; FY27 is described as a portfolio-building year and FY28 as the start of serious business.

segments.name: Carbon Black
segments.commentary: Third-party sales about 10% of the business; Phase II commissioned at Bhuj, lifting capacity to 360,000 MTPA at INR800 crores. Captive power raised to 64 MW (INR125 crores). New business head appointed effective 3 July 2026.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said INR1,500-2,000 crores more will be spent in FY27 on top of INR1,000 crores already spent, and the balance of the INR6,800 crore plan will decline thereafter.

qa_highlights.answer: The CFO-side answer cited a Gujarat minimum-wage increase, staff increments, and hiring for new businesses; management expects this to normalise as new-business turnover builds.

502355|2026-09.headline: BKT signs Pirelli offtake deal to produce 800,000 Pirelli-branded premium car tires per year by 2030 at Bhuj PCR plant, starting CY2027.
502355|2026-09.overview: This was a short business update call on the Pirelli-BKT strategic offtake agreement, held at short notice, with Q2 FY27 performance explicitly off-limits under the silent-period policy. BKT will manufacture Pirelli-branded car tires (17-inch and above) at its newly built Bhuj PCR plant, ramping gradually from CY2027 to 800,000 tires per year by CY2030. A second phase contemplates a 50:50 JV and a dedicated plant for high-value passenger car tires, subject to preset conditions, with management saying the JV work must be announced by 2030. Management said the offtake fits within the existing expansion programme, with no additional capex for the offtake, and pricing is raw material at actuals plus conversion cost.

Roughly 350-355 operating days per year assumed

segments.commentary: Contract manufacturing of Pirelli-branded 17-inch and above car tires at Bhuj, using Pirelli-specific specs; pricing on raw material actuals plus conversion cost, so BKT earns conversion margin. Majority of volume expected for India, with some for Pirelli's global markets.

segments.name: Passenger car tires (PCR) - BKT brand
segments.commentary: Bulk of Phase 1 capacity (about 80% of 6,700 tires/day) stays on BKT brand, addressing the full Indian market from 13-inch upward. BKT is at an early stage of its on-highway journey.

segments.name: Carbon black
segments.commentary: Management said BKT's carbon black business benefits because Pirelli tires made at BKT will use BKT-branded carbon black.

demand_pricing: Pirelli targets the very high-end Indian car market, which management described as about 10% of the total market; Indian passenger car market growing at 6% to 7% annually.

Management declined to share Pirelli's market share in India or the minimum offtake volumes, calling them confidential.

Management said there is no royalty payable in the JV; a separate service agreement covers testing and simulation use of Pirelli infrastructure for BKT-branded products, for a consideration not disclosed.

qa_highlights.question: What investment is needed for the Bhuj capacity and the Pirelli ramp-up?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the offtake is part of the ongoing expansion programme already announced last year; the JV would need additional investment, but no timeline or amount was given.

qa_highlights.question: Will the Pirelli deal be part of the 20% non-OHT revenue target for FY30?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes, Pirelli revenue counts within the existing 20% non-OHT target; management said conviction in the Vision 2030 target has increased.

qa_highlights.answer: No. Management said BKT will use its own technology and designs for its own products, and there will be a clear partition between Pirelli and BKT production.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said there is no royalty and none was discussed. A separate service agreement covers Pirelli testing and simulation infrastructure for BKT products, for consideration.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said distribution stays with each brand's own team; the tie-up is expected to ease channel acceptance for BKT car tires, not to share distribution.

502986|2026-03.headline: Vardhman sees industry spinning spreads near $0.90–0.95/kg versus ~$0.60–0.65 four months ago, but Q4 hit by ~INR57–58 crore forex mark-to-market loss.
502986|2026-03.overview: Management described a sharp turnaround in the Indian textile value chain over the past six months: US tariffs eased, cotton and yarn prices rose, and Chinese yarn demand lifted Indian exports. Q4 gross margin rose about 300 bps QoQ, but EBITDA was held back by an other-expense charge of about INR57–58 crore from mark-to-market on rupee forward cover after the rupee hit INR94.80 on 31 March. Management said fabric price increases lag yarn by 2–3 months, so Q4 did not fully reflect the improvement and Q1 FY27 should be better. The call gave no formal numeric guidance; most outlook comments were qualitative and tied to cotton, the dollar-rupee rate and the FTA pipeline.

financial_highlights.metric: Forex mark-to-market loss charged to other expenses
financial_highlights.change: Q4 one-time hit; rupee at ~INR94.80 on 31 March
Up from ~$0.60–0.65 four months earlier; management cited 40–50% improvement

segments.name: Spinning (yarn)
segments.commentary: 30s combed yarn rose from ~$2.65–2.70/kg in Nov–Dec to ~$3.30–3.35/kg now. Management said yarn prices are set by international cotton and demand is strong, and that spinners are sold about 2–3 months forward in exports.

segments.name: Fabric
segments.commentary: Management said fabric price hikes are being pushed selectively, with a 2–3 month lag to yarn. The new performance (100% synthetic) fabric plant, commissioned last fiscal year, is expected to reach full use in 6–9 months.

segments.name: Garments
segments.commentary: Small existing garment capacity is being expanded to improve viability. Management said there is no decision on a large-scale garment expansion. Average realisation per shirt was stated as $7.5 after an initial misstatement of $5.

guidance_outlook: Management expects most textile companies, including Vardhman, to do far better in Q1 FY27 given the spread improvement, and said Q2 and Q3 should beat last year if current yarn prices, rupee and cotton levels hold.
Remaining ~10% of spinning modernisation to finish in the next 6–8 months; biomass boilers and other green power projects to commission in 1–2 months, with cost benefits from June or July.
Forex mark-to-market will reverse or add depending on where the dollar-rupee closes; no forecast was given.
Cotton: Vardhman normally holds 6–8 months of cotton cover; new Indian crop arrives around October, so stocks must be run down by September.
Management expects FTA-driven demand to build over roughly 12–15 months and is finalising capacity plans over the next 2–3 months.
capex_capacity: Spinning modernisation about 90% complete; remaining work to finish within the current financial year (next 6–8 months).

Performance fabric plant commissioned last fiscal year; 6–9 months needed to build order book. A fourth cotton and normal fabric line was also commissioned in FY26 but could not be fully used because of US tariffs; utilisation is expected in 6–9 months.
Open-end spinning project on hold to restart. New land in PM MITRA Park, Madhya Pradesh is expected by December or January, with plans to be finalised in 2–3 months.

Industry spindles: about 53 million rated; 11–12 million permanently stopped, leaving about 41–42 million working (industry estimate, not government data). Normal additions of 2–2.5 million per year were missed for three years.
Garment capacity expansion approved as a first step to viability; no decision on broader expansion.
demand_pricing: Chinese buying of Indian yarn rose to ~30 million kg per month over the last 4–5 months, against 7–8 million kg earlier. India's monthly yarn exports reached ~120 million kg-plus against a 100 million kg average.

Cotton: New York futures rose from ~$0.62–0.63/lb to ~$0.82–0.83/lb. Indian cotton moved from INR52,000–53,000/candy to INR67,000–68,000/candy; CCI selling price was INR67,000/candy after a ~INR5,000 rise in the last week.
Indian cotton is now priced around New York plus $0.05–0.08, close to the long-run relationship. Management said this removes the earlier disadvantage for spinners.

Pricing: fabric and garment price increases are being pushed across the chain. Brands are granting only small increases so far, with management expecting more clarity in 1–2 months. Yarn cost pass-through was described as comfortable given stronger demand.

Management noted US garment and home textile utilisation has recovered to roughly 90–100% after tariffs eased, from 50–60% earlier. Earlier, US tariffs reached 50%, which had forced discounting and loss-making orders.

qa_highlights.question: How has the cotton price move to parity with US cotton affected yarn demand and realisations?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said yarn prices follow international cotton and that higher Indian cotton cost is absorbed by Indian producers. Demand and higher cotton costs have been passed on comfortably so far.

qa_highlights.question: Can the spread gains be quantified and are they sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management put the spread at ~$0.90–0.95/kg against ~$0.60–0.65 four months earlier, about 40–50% higher. Sustainability depends on New York futures and China demand, which management could not predict.

qa_highlights.question: Why was Q4 EBITDA margin expansion limited despite gross margin gains?
qa_highlights.answer: A ~INR57–58 crore forex mark-to-market charge at INR94.80/USD on export hedges was booked in other expenses. Management said the reversal depends on the year-end rupee rate.

qa_highlights.question: Will Q4 fabric lag mean stronger Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said yes: fabric price increases lag yarn by 2–3 months, and Q1 should be better, with Q2 and Q3 also better than last year if spreads hold.

qa_highlights.question: How long will spindle capacity take to return?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects expansion decisions in 6–9 months if margins hold for 3–6 months. About 1,000 small mills have closed, so consolidation is structural.

qa_highlights.question: What is the plan for garments and realisation per shirt?
qa_highlights.answer: Garment capacity expansion is an early viability step with no decision on broader expansion. Realisation was given as $7.5 per shirt.
